body_text:
## Describe the bug

On Windows, the Explorer context menu item added by Zed ("Open with Zed", localized e.g. 通过 Zed 打开) gets an unintended keyboard shortcut on the letter **e** because the installed menu title contains a misplaced ampersand.

The installer writes `HKCU\Software\Classes\ZedContextMenu\Title` as `通过 Z&ed 打开` (REG_EXPAND_SZ). In Win32 menus `&` marks the mnemonic, so pressing **E** while a file's context menu is open triggers "Open with Zed" (and the title is displayed with "e" underlined). It looks like the ampersand was intended to be before `Z` (`&Zed`, shortcut **Z**) or omitted entirely.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install Zed stable on Windows (e.g. 1.20.2) with default settings.
2. Check `HKCU\Software\Classes\ZedContextMenu\Title` -> `通过 Z&ed 打开`.
3. Right-click a file in Explorer, press **E** while the menu is open -> "Open with Zed" is activated.

## Expected behavior

The menu title should not hijack a common letter as an accelerator. Either place the `&` on `Z` (`通过 &Zed 打开`) or use no ampersand at all.

## Root cause / location

- `script/bundle-windows.ps1` (main): defines `$appShellNameShort = "Z&ed"` for stable, and `"Z&ed Preview"`, `"Z&ed Editor Nightly"`, `"Z&ed Dev"` for preview/nightly/dev.
- `crates/zed/resources/windows/zed.iss`: writes `Software\Classes\{#RegValueName}ContextMenu` -> `Title` = `{cm:OpenWithContextMenu,{#ShellNameShort}}`.
- `crates/explorer_command_injector/src/explorer_command_injector.rs`: `retrieve_command_description()` returns that `Title` verbatim from `IExplorerCommand::GetTitle`, so Explorer interprets `&` as a mnemonic.

## Additional notes

- A full reinstall / repair with the installer rewrites the Title, and the issue returns. In-app updates do not touch it.
- Affects every localized title that includes `{#ShellNameShort}` (observed with zh-CN: `通过 Z&ed 打开`).
- There is no user-facing setting to change or disable this context menu item.
- Workaround: manually set the Title registry value without `&` (user can do this, but installer rewrites it).

## Environment

- Windows 11, Zed stable 1.20.2 (also present on `main` at the time of writing).

**Repository to file at:** https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/new

## Summary

When using an external ACP agent (Kimi Code CLI 0.43.1 via `kimi acp`), session updates start failing en masse after Zed is restarted and an existing agent thread is resumed from history. Every failed update is logged as:

```
ERROR [agent_servers::acp] Failed to handle session update for SessionId("session_f8adf072-..."):
Error { code: -32603: Internal error, message: "Internal error",
data: Some(String("Terminal with id `7cf4c5dd-90ca-4408-a013-bc01993b1259` not found")) }
```

Because the *entire* session update is dropped, user-visible parts of the conversation are lost: chunks of agent/subagent replies never render, tool-call statuses don't update, and the Plan panel stops refreshing (completed tasks never get checked off). Restarting Zed and opening the thread again reloads the content from the agent's own session store, so the "missing" replies become visible — confirming the data existed but the live updates were dropped.

## Environment

- Zed: v1.20.2 (Flathub flatpak, `dev.zed.Zed`, stable)
- OS: Fedora Linux (KDE Plasma), x86_64
- Agent: Kimi Code CLI 0.43.1, launched as a custom agent server:

```json
"agent_servers": {
  "Kimi Code CLI": {
    "type": "custom",
    "command": "/home/saturn/.local/bin/kimi",
    "args": ["acp"],
    "env": { "LD_LIBRARY_PATH": "" }
  }
}
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start an ACP thread with the external agent; let it run commands (agent creates terminals, may leave background tasks running).
2. Restart Zed (or close the window) while the agent session persists on the agent side.
3. Reopen/resume the same thread from history.
4. Continue prompting the agent.

## Expected behavior

- Session updates referencing terminal IDs unknown to the client (e.g. terminals created before a client restart, whose registry is empty) should be handled gracefully: ignore the terminal chunk, re-create the terminal, or at worst skip only the terminal portion.
- Other content in the same update (message chunks, tool-call status, plan entries) must still be applied.

## Actual behavior

Each such update fails with `Terminal with id ... not found` and is **dropped wholesale**. In one log window: 275 occurrences in the current `Zed.log`, 494 in `Zed.log.old`, repeating every ~20–60 seconds for hours as long as the resumed session lives.

Log excerpt (`~/.var/app/dev.zed.Zed/data/zed/logs/Zed.log`):

```
2026-09-19T08:31:12+07:00 ERROR [agent_servers::acp] Failed to handle session update for SessionId("session_f8adf072-e050-45e4-84eb-dc9d34cf44c5"): Error { code: -32603: Internal error, message: "Internal error", data: Some(String("Terminal with id `e92f0681-47f1-494a-b1e3-4f32eaddb3ce` not found")) }
2026-09-19T08:31:37+07:00 ERROR [agent_servers::acp] Failed to handle session update for SessionId("session_f8adf072-e050-45e4-84eb-dc9d34cf44c5"): Error { code: -32603: Internal error, message: "Internal error", data: Some(String("Terminal with id `d20253a4-c1d8-4925-8e52-4271a72ccf51` not found")) }
2026-09-21T15:05:31+07:00 ERROR [agent_servers::acp] Failed to handle session update for SessionId("session_f8adf072-..."): ... "Terminal with id `7cf4c5dd-90ca-4408-a013-bc01993b1259` not found"
```

(The 15:05 burst begins immediately after a Zed restart at 15:02, on a thread created earlier that day.)

## Additional observations

- Harmless but noisy: `fs/read_text_file` requests for non-existent files (e.g. probed `AGENTS.md` paths inside agent task dirs, `/tmp/*.out` files) return `Resource not found` warnings — fine, but shows the agent also delegates file reads through the client.
- Workaround: starting a **new** thread instead of resuming an old one avoids the errors entirely, which points at stale terminal references carried over by session resume.

## Possible fix direction

In `agent_servers::acp` session-update handling, treat an unknown terminal ID as a non-fatal condition (log + skip that chunk) rather than failing the whole update; alternatively re-materialize terminals on `session/load` when the agent references them.

body_text:
### Summary

On startup, while restoring saved agent threads, Zed fails to deserialize tool inputs that were
stored by older versions and logs one `ERROR` per offending call:

```
ERROR [crates/agent/src/thread.rs:1684] missing field `cd`
ERROR [crates/agent/src/thread.rs:1684] missing field `new_text`
ERROR [crates/agent/src/thread.rs:1684] invalid type: null, expected a sequence
```

### Zed version

`1.20.2+stable.360` (latest stable at the time of writing; the schema below is still the same on `main`).

### Root cause

The stored `ToolUse.raw_input` of the terminal tool in these (older) threads is:

```json
{"command": "docker logs ... 2>&1 | grep -i -E \"error|fatal\" ..."}
```

i.e. it predates the `cd` parameter. Today `TerminalToolInput` in
`crates/agent/src/tools/terminal_tool.rs` requires it:

```rust
pub command: String,
pub cd: String,          // required — no #[serde(default)]
pub timeout_ms: Option<u64>,
```

so deserialization fails. `missing field `new_text`` and `invalid type: null, expected a sequence`
are the same class of problem: a stored payload whose shape no longer matches the current struct.
The threads themselves carry `"version": "0.3.0"`, so the data format is versioned — the version
just isn't used to migrate tool inputs on load.

### Impact

History rendering only — the affected tool call is restored without its input details. No crash,
no data loss and no effect on new turns, but it is startup log noise of level `ERROR`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a thread saved by an older Zed whose `terminal` tool call has no `cd` in `raw_input`
   (in my DB: 81 such calls across ~13 threads, dated 2026-06-06 … 2026-07-13).
2. Start Zed.
3. Errors appear right after `workspace: Rendered first frame`, once per offending stored call.

### Suggested fix

- `#[serde(default)]` on `cd` (and audit the other tool-input structs for the same pattern), or
- migrate old thread data on load using the stored `version`, and
- log such mismatches as `warn`/`debug` instead of `error` — a thread that can't restore one old
  tool input is not an error condition for the user.

### Also (minor, separate)

`ERROR [crates/acp_thread/src/diff.rs:37] language not found` is emitted whenever a language
cannot be determined for a file in a diff (unknown or absent extension). Rendering proceeds
without highlighting, so it is a recoverable cosmetic condition, yet it accounted for ~300 lines
in my logs. Worth downgrading to `debug`/`warn`.

On startup, while restoring saved agent threads, Zed fails to deserialize tool inputs that were
stored by older versions and logs one `ERROR` per offending call:

```
ERROR [crates/agent/src/thread.rs:1684] missing field `cd`
ERROR [crates/agent/src/thread.rs:1684] missing field `new_text`
ERROR [crates/agent/src/thread.rs:1684] invalid type: null, expected a sequence
```

### Zed version

`1.20.2+stable.360` (latest stable at the time of writing; the schema below is still the same on `main`).

### Root cause

The stored `ToolUse.raw_input` of the terminal tool in these (older) threads is:

```json
{"command": "docker logs ... 2>&1 | grep -i -E \"error|fatal\" ..."}
```

i.e. it predates the `cd` parameter. Today `TerminalToolInput` in
`crates/agent/src/tools/terminal_tool.rs` requires it:

```rust
pub command: String,
pub cd: String,          // required — no #[serde(default)]
pub timeout_ms: Option<u64>,
```

so deserialization fails. `missing field `new_text`` and `invalid type: null, expected a sequence`
are the same class of problem: a stored payload whose shape no longer matches the current struct.
The threads themselves carry `"version": "0.3.0"`, so the data format is versioned — the version
just isn't used to migrate tool inputs on load.

### Impact

History rendering only — the affected tool call is restored without its input details. No crash,
no data loss and no effect on new turns, but it is startup log noise of level `ERROR`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a thread saved by an older Zed whose `terminal` tool call has no `cd` in `raw_input`
   (in my DB: 81 such calls across ~13 threads, dated 2026-06-06 … 2026-07-13).
2. Start Zed.
3. Errors appear right after `workspace: Rendered first frame`, once per offending stored call.

### Suggested fix

- `#[serde(default)]` on `cd` (and audit the other tool-input structs for the same pattern), or
- migrate old thread data on load using the stored `version`, and
- log such mismatches as `warn`/`debug` instead of `error` — a thread that can't restore one old
  tool input is not an error condition for the user.

### Also (minor, separate)

`ERROR [crates/acp_thread/src/diff.rs:37] language not found` is emitted whenever a language
cannot be determined for a file in a diff (unknown or absent extension). Rendering proceeds
without highlighting, so it is a recoverable cosmetic condition, yet it accounted for ~300 lines
in my logs. Worth downgrading to `debug`/`warn`.

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed
2. Hover over the interface buttons, click them to verify its not flicker.
3. Press any keyboard key and perform step 2 again. You will see the mouse cursor starts flickering and clicking doesn't work on interface items.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current Behavior**:
- Mouse cursor flickering after pressing any keyboard key. It does not matter if the key was pressed while focused in editor or not, and it does not matter if the key was a shortcut or not. Any keyboard key after being pressed causes this behavior. 
- If we use mouse to click buttons, open menus or anything like that, it does not cause flickering.
- Moving focus to different window then refocusing on zed removes the flickering. This refocus has to be done using mouse cursor only. But this flickering comes back from the same keyboard key presses. Refocus does not remove flickering if it was done using keyboard through shortcuts.
- This behavior happens on default settings as well as modified. I will paste my current modified settings.
- Do remember that this mouse cursor flickering does not cause any issues in using shortcuts or typing. It's only an issue for using mouse for hovering and clicking. You can technically still click on something while this issue is happening, but for that, you need to be moving your mouse and then click. And if a hover menu is opened by doing this, the menu does not disappear or flicker, but hovering it's options still flicker. Also, while the hover issue is there, the tooltip won't show as the cursor is flickering like crazy.

**Expected Behavior**:
- No mouse cursor flickering when hovering on interface buttons or options.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: v1.20.2+stable (Zed) 
OS: Linux Wayland arch
Memory: 15.5 GiB
Architecture: x86_64
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (RADV NAVI22) || radv || Mesa 26.2.2-arch1.1

Expected: project panel follows clicked tab.

Maybe relevant:
- This is a regression. Some versions ago, this was working.
- Git panel does follow currently open editor (I'm on a meta-repo).

### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed on Linux.
2. Configure an HTTP proxy in Zed:

> Proxy alow both internet and private range access. May be this is optional, but I cannot try without proxy in my environment.

```json
 {
     "proxy": "http://someproxy:7890"
 }
```
3. Start an Agent Panel conversation.
4. Ask the agent to access an internal HTTP service whose hostname resolves to
an RFC 1918 address. For example:
```bash
   curl --silent --show-error --location \
     http://example.internal.net/
```
DNS resolution for this example is:
```bash
example.internal.net
     CNAME → example.internal.net
     A     → 10.195.6.5
```
5. Approve the agent’s host-scoped network request.
6. Observe that the request fails with HTTP 511.

```bash
HTTP/1.1 511 Network Authentication Required
Via: 1.1 zed-sandbox-proxy
Proxy-Status: zed-sandbox-proxy; error=destination_ip_prohibited;
 details="host example.internal.net'' resolves only to loopback/private/link-local addresses, which sandbox policy blocks"
```

The same behavior occurs when using glab 1.117.0 to access an internal GitLab
instance whose hostname resolves to private addresses



### Current vs. Expected behavior

### Current behavior

Although the hostname is explicitly approved through the agent's host-scoped
network permission, Zed routes the command through an in-process sandbox proxy:

```text
HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<dynamic-port>
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<dynamic-port>
ALL_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<dynamic-port>
NO_PROXY=
no_proxy=
```

The request is rejected with:

```text
HTTP/1.1 511 Network Authentication Required
Via: 1.1 zed-sandbox-proxy
Proxy-Status: zed-sandbox-proxy; error=destination_ip_prohibited;
 details="host 'example.internal.net' resolves only to loopback/private/link-local addresses, which sandbox policy blocks"
```

curl reports that its TCP peer is Zed’s temporary proxy:

```text
remote_ip=127.0.0.1
remote_port=<dynamic-port>
http_code=511
```

When the same command is approved with unrestricted network access, it succeeds:

```text
remote_ip=10.195.6.5
remote_port=80
http_code=200
```

PR #59223 appears to implement the exact rejection being observed:

### Expected behavior

Host-scoped network requests to RFC 1918 Private Ranges addresses succeed, when user approve access.

### Reproduction steps

1. Authenticate to an MCP server
   1. I can repro this 100% of the time with the Atlassian MCP server, but presumably this bug is generic to all servers that return a long token.
2. Authentication fails in Zed with: `Failed to persist OAuth session in keychain: credential for mcp-oauth:<url> is <n> bytes, which exceeds the Windows Credential Manager limit of 2560 bytes`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Due to Windows' limitation, Zed refuses to store the token and the MCP server remains in error, and thus unusable.

I'm not quite sure what the solution is if there's no safe way to store the secret (other than an ugly solution like splitting it up into multiple entries), but leaving the server errored seems like the worst behaviour possible. While annoying, I'd rather the secret be kept in memory and Zed to force me to re-authenticate after each restart, that would at least allow me to use my MCP server instead of having 0 functionality.

body_text: > [!NOTE] > English is not my first language. This report was drafted with AI assistance (Claude), which also inspected the installed files on my machine. I reviewed everything below, verified the findings myself, and confirmed the workaround works. > > *Nota em português: inglês não é minha língua nativa. Este relato foi redigido com ajuda de IA (Claude), que também inspecionou os arquivos instalados na minha máquina. Revisei tudo, conferi os achados pessoalmente e confirmei que o workaround funciona.* Possibly related: #64216 (same pattern with `claude-agent-acp`). ### Reproduction steps 1. Install the Codex agent from the ACP registry. 2. Open a new Codex thread in the agent panel. 3. The agent shows "Failed to Launch" (error below). Clicking Retry fails the same way. 4. Uninstall and reinstall the agent: same error. There is no option in the UI to sign out, re-authenticate or force a clean reinstall. ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current behavior:** Codex fails to launch with: ``` Codex process has exited with code 1: file:///Users//Library/Application%20Support/Zed/external_agents/registry/npx/codex-acp/node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js:107 throw new Error( ^ Error: Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-darwin-arm64. Reinstall Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex@latest at findCodexExecutable (file:///.../node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js:107:9) at file:///.../node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js:112:20 at ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:569:25) at async node:internal/modules/esm/loader:650:26 at async asyncRunEntryPointWithESMLoader (node:internal/modules/run_main:101:5) Node.js v26.8.1 ``` The error message is misleading: the platform package **is** installed, but its native binary is missing. - `~/Library/Application Support/Zed/external_agents/registry/npx/codex-acp/package.json` → `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@1.13.1` - `node_modules/@openai/codex` → `0.156.1` - `node_modules/@openai/codex-darwin-arm64` → `0.156.1-darwin-arm64` is present, but `vendor/aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/` contains only `codex-code-mode-host`. The `codex` binary that `codex.js` looks for (`vendor/aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/codex`) does not exist. So the install ended up incomplete, and Zed keeps reusing the broken `node_modules`, because uninstalling/reinstalling the agent does not clear that directory. **Expected behavior:** - When an agent fails to launch, Zed should offer a way to reinstall it cleanly (wipe `external_agents/registry/npx/`) and/or sign out and re-authenticate. - Uninstalling an agent should remove its installed files, so a reinstall starts from scratch. **Workaround:** quit Zed, delete the agent's install directory, reopen Zed. It reinstalls the agent and Codex works again. ``` rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/Zed/external_agents/registry/npx/codex-acp ``` ### Zed version and system specs - Zed: 1.21.0 - OS: macOS 27.0 (26A428) - Architecture: aarch64 (Apple Silicon) - Node.js: v26.8.1 (arm64), npm 11.19.0 - codex-acp: 1.13.1, @openai/codex: 0.156.1

### Reproduction steps

1. Use Claude Code as an external agent over ACP (`agent_servers.claude-acp`).
2. Get it to produce a response containing `<cc-memory filenames="...">...</cc-memory>`.  It emits these when citing its persistent memory. Merely *mentioning* the literal string is enough, including inside a fenced code block.
3. Observe the response in the agent panel.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** 
The message renders twice, concatenated:

- **First copy:** raw markup visible, e.g. `<cc-memory filenames="reference_result_seeding.md">` appears as literal text. Often visibly truncated.
- **Second copy**: Complete, with the tags stripped. Inside code blocks the tag text is simply removed, leaving a gap (` containing  tags : 10` where the source said ` containing <cc-memory> tags : 10`).

**Expected:**
The message renders once, with the `<cc-memory>` markup stripped.

## Reproduction steps

Not reliably reproducible yet — happened once. Observed conditions:

1. Zed was running for ~5.5 days (launched 2026-09-19) and had auto-updated to v1.21.0 a few hours before the crash.
2. ~15 minutes before the crash, Zed.log flooded with `filesystem watcher lost sync for many files` warnings (an external Thunderbolt drive may have been disconnected around that time), followed by ~15 minutes of log silence.
3. While typing with Google Japanese Input (`com.google.inputmethod.Japanese`) active, Zed was killed instantly by a SIGTRAP.

The crash is raised inside Apple frameworks; no Zed code appears in the crashing path. It looks like an AppKit assertion (`CFEqual() called with NULL second argument`) fired while AppKit was building the attributed string for marked text (`-[NSTextInputContext _forceAttributedString]`) during an IME `setMarkedText` / `selectedRange` round-trip.

Top of the crashing stack (Thread 0, main thread, input method `com.google.inputmethod.Japanese`):

```
0   CoreFoundation  CFEqual.cold.1 + 16
1   CoreFoundation  CFEqual + 956
2   AppKit          -[NSTextInputContext _forceAttributedString] + 60
3   AppKit          __55-[NSTextInputContext handleTSMEvent:completionHandler:]_block_invoke_3.232 + 676
```

- Exception Type: EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
- Application Specific Information: `*** CFEqual() called with NULL second argument ***`
- No Zed panic/minidump was produced (the OS trap killed the process before Zed's crash handler could act).
- A Zed MCP child process (`bun-docs-mcp-proxy`) aborted ~34 s later (SIGABRT), presumably a cascade from Zed's death.

Next step to narrow it down: switch to the built-in Japanese IME to see whether the crash is specific to Google Japanese Input.

## Zed version and system specs

- Zed: v1.21.0 (build 20260923.151803)
- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)
- Memory: 48 GiB
- Architecture: aarch64
- Hardware: Mac16,8
- Input method: Google Japanese Input 3.34.6260

## Zed log

The crash itself produced no log entry (killed by the trap). The last entries before the ~15-minute silence preceding the crash were a flood of:

```log
2026-09-24T07:25:39+09:00 WARN  [fs::fs_watcher] filesystem watcher lost sync for many files, not logging more
```

The complete `.ips` crash report and the relevant log window are available on request.

3. While typing with Google Japanese Input (`com.google.inputmethod.Japanese`) active, Zed was killed instantly by a SIGTRAP.

The crash is raised inside Apple frameworks; no Zed code appears in the crashing path. It looks like an AppKit assertion (`CFEqual() called with NULL second argument`) fired while AppKit was building the attributed string for marked text (`-[NSTextInputContext _forceAttributedString]`) during an IME `setMarkedText` / `selectedRange` round-trip.

Top of the crashing stack (Thread 0, main thread, input method `com.google.inputmethod.Japanese`):

```
0   CoreFoundation  CFEqual.cold.1 + 16
1   CoreFoundation  CFEqual + 956
2   AppKit          -[NSTextInputContext _forceAttributedString] + 60
3   AppKit          __55-[NSTextInputContext handleTSMEvent:completionHandler:]_block_invoke_3.232 + 676
```

- Exception Type: EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
- Application Specific Information: `*** CFEqual() called with NULL second argument ***`
- No Zed panic/minidump was produced (the OS trap killed the process before Zed's crash handler could act).
- A Zed MCP child process (`bun-docs-mcp-proxy`) aborted ~34 s later (SIGABRT), presumably a cascade from Zed's death.

Next step to narrow it down: switch to the built-in Japanese IME to see whether the crash is specific to Google Japanese Input.

## Zed version and system specs

- Zed: v1.21.0 (build 20260923.151803)
- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)
- Memory: 48 GiB
- Architecture: aarch64
- Hardware: Mac16,8
- Input method: Google Japanese Input 3.34.6260

## Zed log

The crash itself produced no log entry (killed by the trap). The last entries before the ~15-minute silence preceding the crash were a flood of:

```log
2026-09-24T07:25:39+09:00 WARN  [fs::fs_watcher] filesystem watcher lost sync for many files, not logging more
```

The complete `.ips` crash report and the relevant log window are available on request.

### Reproduction steps

Use Ctrl + Left/Right to move the cursor, or the shortcut to select words

### Current vs. Expected behavior

When using Ctrl + Left/Right, the cursor will usually go way further than it would make sense.
For example, in this example:
```papyrus
Function MyFunction()
    SomeScript.DoSomething()
|EndFunction
```
with the cursor at the start of "EndFunction", using ctrl+left would make the cursor move before the function brackets:
```papyrus
Function MyFunction()
    SomeScript.DoSomething|()
EndFunction
```
While the expected behavior would be the cursor going to the end of the line:
```papyrus
Function MyFunction()
    SomeScript.DoSomething()|
EndFunction
```

This is not specific to any language, it applies to virtually any language.

Outside of vscode (which has the exact same issue as zed), any editor/ide i've used so far (windows notepad, notepad++, any jetbrains ide's) would do this the "expected" way.

### Reproduction steps

1. On macOS, use pyenv 2.7.3 with zsh and initialize it in ~/.zshrc via pyenv init.
2. Open Zed 1.21.0 and ask the built-in Agent to run a trivial command such as true using its terminal tool.
3. Repeat with another command.

### Current vs. expected behavior

Every agent terminal invocation prints this line before the command output, even for true (which does not use Python):

    pyenv: shell integration not enabled. Run `pyenv init` for instructions.

Expected: Running an unrelated command through the Agent terminal tool should not produce a pyenv warning.

This reproduces consistently in this installation. Running /bin/sh -ic true separately inside the terminal does not print an additional warning. Calling pyenv shell --unset in that shell produces the same warning, but I cannot confirm whether that is the command Zed runs.

### Environment / observations

- Zed: 1.21.0 (stable)
- macOS: 27.0, arm64
- pyenv: 2.7.3
- Agent terminal process observed as /bin/sh -i -c, while the inherited SHELL is /bin/zsh and PYENV_SHELL is zsh.
- ~/.zshrc already initializes pyenv. No terminal or Python environment overrides in Zed settings.json.
- No personal settings or logs attached; I can provide sanitized diagnostics if needed.

### Model provider details

- Provider: OpenAI (Zed built-in Agent)
- Model: GPT-6-Sol
- Mode: Agent Panel, terminal tool

while [alt]+[left] and [alt]+[right] "hop" a word and [alt]+[backspace] properly deletes leftward [alt]+[right]

### Reproduction steps

1. In the Agent Panel, configure two providers with thinking enabled:
   - Claude with thinking (e.g. Claude 3.7 Sonnet / Claude Opus with thinking via `anthropic_compatible` or Anthropic API)
   - Google AI with `gemini-3.8-flash` (or `gemini-3.7-flash`), `mode: thinking`
2. Start a new agent thread with the Claude model and ask a question that exercises thinking and tool execution (e.g. "Read the files in this project and inspect the architecture").
3. Wait for the turn to complete. Claude's assistant message now contains a thinking block with an encrypted thinking signature.
4. Switch the thread's model to **Gemini 3.8 Flash** in the top model dropdown.
5. Send any follow-up message (e.g. "Now run tests").

**Additional trigger paths (without manual model switching):**
- **Title generation:** If the default or summarization model is Gemini with thinking, automatic title generation on Claude threads fails with this error.
- **Compaction:** If `agent.compaction_model` is set to a Gemini thinking model (e.g. `gemini-3.7-flash`), auto-compaction or manual compaction on Claude threads fails with this error.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior:**
Google immediately rejects the request with HTTP 400:
```json
failed to stream completion: error during streamGenerateContent, status code: 400, body: {
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Invalid thought signature.",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT"
  }
}
```
The thread is completely bricked for Gemini. Every subsequent message, title generation, and compaction attempt fails with this error.

**Expected behavior:**
When switching models or using a cross-provider compaction/summarization model, the thread should continue functioning. Provider-specific encrypted tokens (such as thinking signatures and tool thought signatures) should only be replayed to the provider that issued them.

### Cause & Analysis

In Zed, thread messages are represented as generic `AgentMessageContent::Thinking { text, signature }` without tracking which provider issued the signature. 

When building history for Google (`crates/google_ai/src/completion.rs::into_google`), Zed forwards all stored signatures directly into Google's `thoughtSignature` field:

```rust
MessageContent::Thinking { text, signature: Some(signature) } => {
    if !signature.is_empty() {
        mapped_parts.push(Part::TextPart(TextPart {
            text,
            thought: true,
            thought_signature: Some(signature), // <-- Forwards Claude's encrypted signature to Google!
        }));
    }
}
```

Google attempts to decrypt and validate the foreign signature against its own cryptographic keys, fails verification, and hard-rejects the request with `400: Invalid thought signature.`

### Suggested Fix

Thinking signatures and tool-call thought signatures are opaque tokens that can only be validated by the issuing provider.

1. **Track producing provider on `AgentMessage`:**
   Add `provider: Option<LanguageModelProviderId>` to `AgentMessage` (with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` for backwards compatibility with existing stored threads in `threads.db`). Set it from `model.upstream_provider_id()` when `pending_message` is created.

2. **Filter signatures centrally when building request history:**
   In `extend_request_history_until` / `AgentMessage::to_request_for_provider`, pass the target model's `upstream_provider_id()`. If an assistant message originated from a different provider:
   - Strip `Thinking` and `RedactedThinking` parts and `reasoning_details`.
   - Strip `thought_signature` from `ToolUse` parts (keep `name`, `input`, and `tool_results` intact).
   - This single change in `extend_request_history_until` cleanly covers normal turns, auto-compaction (`build_compaction_request`), title generation (`build_thread_title_request`), and detailed summaries (`summary()`).
   - It also protects the reverse direction (Gemini signatures replayed into Anthropic).

3. **Backwards compatibility:**
   Messages saved prior to recording `provider` have `provider: None`. When targeting a thinking model, their signatures are omitted rather than risking sending incompatible tokens.

*(Note: I verified this fix live against real Gemini API calls — filtering foreign signatures allows bricked threads to resume and complete compaction without issue. I also implemented and verified the `thread.rs` changes locally with all `agent` and `sidebar` unit tests passing).*

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: 1.21.0
OS: macOS 14.7.6
Architecture: aarch64

### Attach Zed log file

<details><summary>Zed.log</summary>

```log
2026-09-24T14:28:49+02:00 ERROR [agent::thread] failed to generate thread title: failed to stream completion: error during streamGenerateContent, status code: 400, body: {
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Invalid thought signature.",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT"
  }
}

2026-09-24T14:31:24+02:00 ERROR [agent::thread] Turn execution failed: failed to stream completion

Caused by:
    error during streamGenerateContent, status code: 400, body: {
      "error": {
        "code": 400,
        "message": "Invalid thought signature.",
        "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT"
      }
    }
```

</details>

### Relevant Zed settings

<details><summary>settings.json</summary>

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "default_model": {
      "provider": "google",
      "model": "gemini-3.8-flash"
    },
    "compaction_model": {
      "provider": "google",
      "model": "gemini-3.7-flash"
    }
  }
}
```

</details>

- Provider: Google AI via API Key + Anthropic Claude (via `anthropic_compatible` / Vertex AI)
- Model Name: `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.7-flash`, `claude-opus-5-5` / `claude-3-7-sonnet`
- Mode: Agent Panel (manual model switch, title generation, and auto-compaction)

Thinking signatures and tool-call thought signatures are opaque tokens that can only be validated by the issuing provider.

1. **Track producing provider on `AgentMessage`:**
   Add `provider: Option<LanguageModelProviderId>` to `AgentMessage` (with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` for backwards compatibility with existing stored threads in `threads.db`). Set it from `model.upstream_provider_id()` when `pending_message` is created.

2. **Filter signatures centrally when building request history:**
   In `extend_request_history_until` / `AgentMessage::to_request_for_provider`, pass the target model's `upstream_provider_id()`. If an assistant message originated from a different provider:
   - Strip `Thinking` and `RedactedThinking` parts and `reasoning_details`.
   - Strip `thought_signature` from `ToolUse` parts (keep `name`, `input`, and `tool_results` intact).
   - This single change in `extend_request_history_until` cleanly covers normal turns, auto-compaction (`build_compaction_request`), title generation (`build_thread_title_request`), and detailed summaries (`summary()`).
   - It also protects the reverse direction (Gemini signatures replayed into Anthropic).

3. **Backwards compatibility:**
   Messages saved prior to recording `provider` have `provider: None`. When targeting a thinking model, their signatures are omitted rather than risking sending incompatible tokens.

*(Note: I verified this fix live against real Gemini API calls — filtering foreign signatures allows bricked threads to resume and complete compaction without issue. I also implemented and verified the `thread.rs` changes locally with all `agent` and `sidebar` unit tests passing).*

## Summary

When a thread's LLM-generated title was never produced (e.g. title generation silently failed with a custom/OpenAI-compatible provider), the sidebar keeps showing the provisional first-message title — until the user **opens the thread once**. Opening re-saves the sidebar metadata with the thread's *real* title (empty), wiping the provisional title, so the row degrades to **"New Agent Thread"**. Meanwhile the opened thread view itself still renders a first-message-derived title, so the title appears to "disappear from the list but exist inside the thread".

## Environment

- Zed 1.21.0 (`33c95853ed2b6956f339733c63a8220964ecbeb6`), stable
- Windows 11
- Model: custom OpenAI-compatible proxy (title generation fails/returns empty for some threads; succeeds intermittently for others)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a model where automatic thread-title generation fails (e.g. a proxy that errors on the summarization request), or otherwise end the first turn without a generated title.
2. Start a thread, send a first message, let the turn finish. The sidebar row shows the provisional title (derived from the first user message).
3. Click the thread in the sidebar to open it.
4. Observe the sidebar row now reads "New Agent Thread" — permanently, even after closing the thread. The thread view header still shows a title derived from the first message.

## Expected

The sidebar row should keep showing the provisional/fallback title (as the thread view does), or at minimum re-derive it on load; a failed/absent LLM title must not *erase* an already-displayed fallback.

## Actual

The sidebar metadata title is overwritten with the empty real title on open, and never recovers.

## Evidence (local DB forensics)

Two stores are involved:

1. `~/.local/share/zed/threads/threads.db` (native `Thread` store, zstd-compressed JSON `data` blob + `summary` column). For the affected threads, the persisted `title` is `""` — auto-title generation never completed:

   ```text
   45a04490 | stored_title='' | first user msg='看看 我本地 zed 占用了多少 RAM'  (17 messages)
   b633d87e | stored_title='' | first user msg='dws'                             (26 messages)
   7fcdf684 | stored_title='' | first user msg='今天有什么AI大事件？'              (11 messages)
   ...
   ```

   (Threads where title generation *did* succeed have real titles in both stores, e.g. "Terminal Execution Failure Troubleshooting".)

2. The sidebar reads `sidebar_threads.title` from the main state DB (`db/0-stable/db.sqlite`, `ThreadMetadataDb`). The correlation between "opened" and "wiped" is exact — every row whose title is now `''` was `updated_at` at the moment I clicked it, while unopened rows still carry the first-message text:

   ```text
   ac83c095 | title='今天有什么新闻AI相关的大事件' | (not opened)   <- provisional survived
   b633d87e | title='dws'                          | (not opened)   <- provisional survived
   45a04490 | title=''                             | opened 01:42   <- wiped
   7fcdf684 | title=''                             | opened 01:31   <- wiped
   35105982 | title=''                             | opened 01:42   <- wiped
   319a0cde | title=''                             | opened 01:42   <- wiped
   4ed532a9 | title=''                             | opened 01:43   <- wiped
   ```

## Root cause (from source at the release commit)

- `AcpThread` has two title fields; the fallback is a *provisional* title set only in the live session:

  `crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs`
  ```rust
  pub fn title(&self) -> Option<SharedString> {
      self.title.clone().or_else(|| self.provisional_title.clone())
  }

  /// Sets a provisional display title without propagating back to the
  /// underlying agent connection. This is used for quick preview titles
  /// (e.g. first 20 chars of the user message) ...
  pub fn set_provisional_title(...)
  ```

- The provisional title is **not re-derived when a thread is loaded from the database** (the native `Thread` restores `title: None` for empty DB titles, see `Thread::from_db` in `crates/agent/src/thread.rs`), so after a reload `AcpThread::title()` returns `None`.

### Reproduction steps

Follow-up to #64577 (fixed by #64683).

### Problem

`Buffer::build` doesn't accept a `LanguageRegistry`, and `set_language` /
`set_language_async` don't require one. The registry is attached separately via
`Buffer::set_language_registry` → `SyntaxMap::set_language_registry`, where it
is `Option`. Nothing enforces the pairing.

When the registry is missing, injection resolution silently fails: block-level
captures highlight normally while injected grammars (Markdown-Inline, fenced
code block languages) produce no captures and no error. This is how #64577
went unnoticed — the git commit view assigned a language without a registry.

### Known affected path

- `crates/acp_thread/src/diff.rs:279-281` builds a buffer and sets a language
  without attaching a registry — same shape as the pre-fix `commit_view.rs`.
  ACP diff views of Markdown files likely show the same unstyled injections.

### Proposed directions

- Make the registry mandatory in `Buffer::build` (or add a
  `build_with_language` constructor taking both), or
- Have `set_language` require/carry the registry, or
- At minimum, `debug_assert!` when a language with injections is set on a
  buffer with no registry.

### Blast radius

Most call sites already attach the registry (`buffer_store`, `lsp_store`,
`git_store`, `text_diff_view`, `repl_editor`, `agent_ui`), so migration is
mechanical, but it touches ~10+ crates — hence a separate structural change
rather than part of the #64577 bug fix.

### Acceptance criteria

- Assigning a language without a registry is a compile error (or debug panic).
- `acp_thread/src/diff.rs` path fixed.
- No regressions in existing buffer/syntax-map tests.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** A `Buffer` can be assigned a language via `set_language` /
`set_language_async` without a `LanguageRegistry` ever being attached:
`Buffer::build` doesn't accept one, and `SyntaxMap`'s registry is an `Option`
set separately via `set_language_registry`. In that state, injection resolution
silently fails — the outer language parses and highlights, but injected
grammars (Markdown-Inline, fenced code block languages) produce no layers, no
captures, and no error or log.

Observed instance: #64577 — git-history buffers rendered Markdown with every
inline capture (`emphasis`, `strong`, `link_uri`, `text.literal`) unstyled
while block-level captures (`title`, `punctuation.list_marker`) worked. Fixed
point-wise in #64683, but the API still permits the same mistake.

Second instance (by code inspection, not yet UI-verified):
`crates/acp_thread/src/diff.rs:279-281` builds a diff buffer and sets a
language without attaching a registry — Markdown diffs in ACP threads likely
show the same unstyled injections.

**Expected:** The buffer/language API makes this state impossible — e.g.
`Buffer::build` requires the registry, or `set_language` requires it — so the
pairing is enforced at compile time (or at minimum via `debug_assert!`) rather
than by convention at every call site.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: v1.21.0+nightly.bf921d03b88df7cecb7b693690ce5862be6f5785 (Zed Nightly bf921d03b88df7cecb7b693690ce5862be6f5785)

Observed instance: #64577 — git-history buffers rendered Markdown with every
inline capture (`emphasis`, `strong`, `link_uri`, `text.literal`) unstyled
while block-level captures (`title`, `punctuation.list_marker`) worked. Fixed
point-wise in #64683, but the API still permits the same mistake.

Second instance (by code inspection, not yet UI-verified):
`crates/acp_thread/src/diff.rs:279-281` builds a diff buffer and sets a
language without attaching a registry — Markdown diffs in ACP threads likely
show the same unstyled injections.

**Expected:** The buffer/language API makes this state impossible — e.g.
`Buffer::build` requires the registry, or `set_language` requires it — so the
pairing is enforced at compile time (or at minimum via `debug_assert!`) rather
than by convention at every call site.

body_text:
## Problem

When a variable font is registered with `cx.add_fonts` (a single face covering a weight range, e.g. wght 300-700), styling text with `FontWeight::BOLD` has no effect: everything renders at weight 400.

## Repro

1. Register a variable font (e.g. Space Grotesk variable, wght 300-700) via `add_fonts`.
2. Render text with `.font_family(...)` + `.font_weight(FontWeight::BOLD)`.
3. Observe: the glyphs render at 400.

## Root cause

Checked against gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.6 (`src/cosmic_text_system.rs`):

1. `load_family` instantiates the font handle with `get_font(database_id, cosmic_text::Weight::NORMAL)` (~line 412). A variable font is a single face in the fontdb, so this pins the swash outlines at 400.
2. At shaping time, `font_match_properties` builds the cosmic-text `Attrs` from `face.weight` (the weight recorded in the fontdb, 400 for the variable default instance) instead of the `FontRun`'s requested weight (see `layout_line_no_separators`). So cosmic-text is told weight 400 and handed 400 outlines. The requested weight never reaches shaping.

The selection side does know about weight (`font_id` -> `find_best_match` scores candidates by weight difference), which is why static per-weight faces mostly work. The break is specific to variable fonts.

## Why it matters

Anyone bundling a variable font for brand typography currently cannot use weight for hierarchy at all. The workaround is vendoring static instances as separate families and pointing headings at them explicitly.

1. Register a variable font (e.g. Space Grotesk variable, wght 300-700) via `add_fonts`.
2. Render text with `.font_family(...)` + `.font_weight(FontWeight::BOLD)`.
3. Observe: the glyphs render at 400.

## Root cause

Checked against gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.6 (`src/cosmic_text_system.rs`):

1. `load_family` instantiates the font handle with `get_font(database_id, cosmic_text::Weight::NORMAL)` (~line 412). A variable font is a single face in the fontdb, so this pins the swash outlines at 400.
2. At shaping time, `font_match_properties` builds the cosmic-text `Attrs` from `face.weight` (the weight recorded in the fontdb, 400 for the variable default instance) instead of the `FontRun`'s requested weight (see `layout_line_no_separators`). So cosmic-text is told weight 400 and handed 400 outlines. The requested weight never reaches shaping.

The selection side does know about weight (`font_id` -> `find_best_match` scores candidates by weight difference), which is why static per-weight faces mostly work. The break is specific to variable fonts.

## Why it matters

Anyone bundling a variable font for brand typography currently cannot use weight for hierarchy at all. The workaround is vendoring static instances as separate families and pointing headings at them explicitly.

### Reproduction steps

1. Open a Git repository in Zed with at least one modified tracked file.

2. Open the Git panel.

3. Click a modified tracked file in the Changes list.
   - Zed opens the file's diff in the editor.
   - The file remains selected in the Git panel.
   - Using "dev: open key context view" shows the Git panel / ChangesList as the innermost active context.

4. Press Backspace.
   - Instead of acting on the selected Git panel item, focus/context switches to the editor.
   - The character before the editor cursor is deleted.

5. Repeat with Cmd+Backspace.
   - Again, the context switches from the Git panel to the editor.
   - The editor's Cmd+Backspace action runs instead, deleting text to the beginning of the line.

There is already a default Git panel keybinding for:

git: restore file
{"skip_prompt": true}

with a context similar to:

GitPanel && ChangesList && !GitBranchSelector ...

and the shortcut shown is Cmd+Delete.

On a MacBook, pressing Cmd + the Delete/Backspace key does not trigger "Git: Restore File" in this situation because the input appears to be routed to the editor instead.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

## Current behavior

The Git panel initially has focus and is shown as the innermost key context.

As soon as Backspace or Cmd+Backspace is pressed, the active context switches to the editor and the corresponding editor command is executed:

- Backspace deletes the character before the cursor.
- Cmd+Backspace deletes text toward the beginning of the line.

As a result, the existing Git panel "Git: Restore File" keybinding cannot be triggered using the expected MacBook Delete/Backspace key while a changed file is selected.

## Expected behavior
When a tracked file is selected in GitPanel > ChangesList and a Git-panel-specific shortcut such as Delete / Backspace is pressed, the key event should remain in the Git panel context and trigger "Git: Restore File" for the selected file.

At minimum, pressing Backspace or Cmd+Backspace should not unexpectedly transfer keyboard focus into the editor and execute an editor deletion command when the Git panel is the active/innermost context.


## Related behavior

Selecting a changed file in the Git panel opens its diff. Running "Git: Restore" (Cmd+Option+Z) restores the selected diff hunk, but the file remains listed as changed until I press Cmd+S.

After saving, the file disappears from the Git panel.

This may or may not be related, but it suggests the Git panel / project diff / editor focus and buffer state may be interacting unexpectedly.

### Reproduction steps


### Summary

When an integrated terminal process exits normally with `exit`, Zed does not restore keyboard focus to the previously focused editor.

The editor remains visible and otherwise functional, but the text caret is not visible and the editor does not appear to have keyboard focus.

Interestingly, simply moving the mouse over the workspace is enough to restore the editor focus/caret. Running the `editor: toggle focus` command also immediately restores it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a file in Zed so that the editor has focus.
2. Open an integrated terminal using the default shortcut.
3. In the terminal, run:

```sh
exit
```

4. The terminal closes as expected.
5. Observe the editor.

### Actual behavior

After the terminal exits:

* The terminal disappears normally.
* The editor remains visible.
* The editor does not have keyboard focus.
* The text caret is not visible.
* Keyboard input does not appear to be directed to the editor.

However, the focus can be restored immediately by either:

* moving the mouse over the Zed workspace, without clicking; or
* running `editor: toggle focus` from the Command Palette.

For example:

```text
Terminal
  ↓
exit
  ↓
Terminal disappears
  ↓
Editor is visible, but no caret/focus
  ↓
Move mouse
  ↓
Editor immediately gets focus/caret
```

The same behavior occurs when opening a terminal through the terminal panel toggle as well as when creating a new terminal.

### Expected behavior

When the terminal process exits, focus should automatically return to the previously focused editor, and the editor caret should become visible immediately.

In other words:

```text
Editor → Terminal → exit → Editor (focused)
```

### Additional observations

This does not appear to be a complete application/window focus loss.

For example, immediately after the terminal exits:

* `Cmd+P` still opens the Command Palette.
* The Command Palette itself receives focus normally.
* After closing the Command Palette, the editor regains focus.
* `editor: toggle focus` restores the editor immediately.
* Merely moving the mouse is also sufficient to make the editor caret appear again.

This makes the issue appear to be related specifically to the focus state after the terminal view/process is removed, rather than the Zed window losing OS-level focus.

### Zed version

Zed 1.21.0

### OS

macOS

### Keymap

Default Zed keybindings.

### Workaround

Currently, moving the mouse over the workspace or invoking `editor: toggle focus` restores the editor focus.

### Expected result

The editor should automatically regain focus after the terminal process exits without requiring any additional mouse movement, command, or click.


### Current vs. Expected behavior

### Current behavior
﻿
After running `exit` in the integrated terminal, the terminal disappears, but the editor does not regain keyboard focus.
﻿
The editor remains visible, but the caret becomes inactive or disappears. The editor does not automatically regain focus after the terminal process exits.
﻿
The editor can be focused again by simply moving the mouse over the workspace, without clicking, or by running `editor: focus`. Opening and closing the Command Palette with `Cmd+P` also restores the editor focus.
﻿
### Expected behavior
﻿
After the integrated terminal process exits and the terminal disappears, the editor should automatically regain keyboard focus.
﻿
The caret should immediately become active, and the editor should be ready to receive keyboard input without requiring any additional mouse movement, clicking, or focus-related commands.

### Reproduction steps

1. `git clone https://github.com/yump/devcontainer_localEnv.git`, or otherwise create a folder containing a minimal Devcontainer setup that uses `localEnv`:

    `test/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`:

    ```json
    {
      "name": "test",
      "build": {
        "context": "..",
        "dockerfile": "Dockerfile",
      },
      "runArgs": [
         "--add-host",
          "${localEnv:HOSTNAME}:host-gateway",
      ],
    }
    ```

    `test/.devcontainer/Dockerfile`:

    ```
    FROM alpine:3.20

    CMD ["echo", "Hello, World!"]
    ```

2. `zed test/`
3. Say yes when prompted to create the dev container.  
4. Close Zed.
5. Destroy the container with `podman rm --latest --force`.
6. Re-launch Zed with `zed --new`. ([Bare `zed` will not work because it tries to reconnect to the non-running container](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/59347).)
7. Open the local folder from recent projects, or by selecting it again in the file picker.
8. Say yes when prompted to create the dev container. Observe failure. Close zed.
9. Repeat steps 2 and 3. Observe success.

In my reproduction repo, there's a podman wrapper script that logs how podman is being called to files in `/tmp/`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior: log message indicates that podman is called with `--add-host :host-gateway`, instead of `--add-host fedora-dev-sandbox:host-gateway`, but only when the project is opened from the GUI. Podman is called correctly when the project path is a command line argument to `zed`.

Expected behavior: localEnv is interpolated correctly no matter how the project is opened.

      },
      "runArgs": [
         "--add-host",
          "${localEnv:HOSTNAME}:host-gateway",
      ],
    }
    ```

    `test/.devcontainer/Dockerfile`:

    ```
    FROM alpine:3.20

    CMD ["echo", "Hello, World!"]
    ```

2. `zed test/`
3. Say yes when prompted to create the dev container.  
4. Close Zed.
5. Destroy the container with `podman rm --latest --force`.
6. Re-launch Zed with `zed --new`. ([Bare `zed` will not work because it tries to reconnect to the non-running container](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/59347).)

body_text: ### Reproduction steps 1. Install two monospace fonts: one **without** CJK coverage (e.g. JetBrains Mono / Zed Mono) and one **with** CJK coverage (e.g. [Maple Mono NF CN](https://github.com/subframe7536/maple-font)). 2. In `settings.json`, let CJK come from `buffer_font_fallbacks` — i.e. `buffer_font_family` itself has no CJK glyphs: ```json { "buffer_font_family": "JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono", "buffer_font_fallbacks": ["Maple Mono Normal NF CN"], "theme": { "mode": "dark", "dark": "Catppuccin Mocha", "light": "Catppuccin Latte" } } ``` (Zed's built-in Catppuccin themes set `syntax.comment.font_style: "italic"`, so comments render italic — any theme with italic comments triggers this.) 3. Open a `.rs` file containing a CJK comment, e.g. `// 待应用的更新：查到更新后先下载，用户点"立即更新"（或下次启动）再应用重启`. 4. → The comment renders correctly the first time (screenshot 1 below). 5. Quit Zed completely, start it again, and reopen the same file. 6. → The Chinese characters inside the italic comments are now drawn with **wrong, mismatched glyphs** — they look like random other CJK characters, not tofu boxes. Non-italic code, Latin words inside the same comments, and string literals still render fine. ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current behavior**: after a restart, CJK characters that are resolved through `buffer_font_fallbacks` are rendered with the wrong glyphs whenever the enclosing text style is italic. Same file, same settings — only the restart differs. Screenshot 1 — right after applying the settings (correct): Screenshot 2 — identical file and settings, after restarting Zed (garbled): **Expected behavior**: CJK characters coming from a fallback font should keep their normal glyphs (real or synthetic italic) after a restart, exactly as they do before it. **Additional observations** - If the CJK font is used as `buffer_font_family` directly (no fallback involved), the bug does not occur, even with italic comments. - Only italic text is affected; non-italic CJK text renders fine. - The Maple Mono author reproduced it independently on Windows and reached the same conclusion: the trigger is *the font in `buffer_font_family` has no CJK glyphs* + *italic comment* + *restart* → garbled. ### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed
2. Select a local project
3. Start a new agent thread
4. Enter a simple prompt (see attached file)
5. After the agent has been running for a moment, an error message appears stating that the maximum context size (1M tokens) has been exceeded for the model being used (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash)
6. Start a completely new agent thread (to reset the context window)
7. Enter the same prompt
8. Get the same error
Note: This problem occurs only occasionally, but it has happened to me several times over the past month.

[thread-log.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32696280/thread-log.md)

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior: Even with very simple prompts, I get an error indicating that the maximum context length (1M tokens) has been exceeded.
Expected behavior: The agent works without errors.

### Zed version and system specs

### Reproduction steps

1. Make sure you have at least one LLM configured in your Zed settings.
2.  Open Zed in an empty folder
3. Create six markdown files: `chapter1.md` containing `Content 1`, then `chapter2.md` containing `Content 2`, ..., finally `chapter6.md` containing `Content 6`.
4. Open the agent panel.
5. Make sure you have a fresh Zed agent thread in the agent panel. If not, click on the `+` symbol at the top and start a fresh Zed agent.
6. Make sure you have an LLM selected in the agent panel status bar.
7. Submit the following prompt: `Read chapter1 through chapter6. Report the content number you find in each of the 6 chapters.`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

# Current behavior

LLM reports (excerpt)

> | Chapter | Content number |
> |---------|----------------|
> | `chapter1.md` | 3 |
> | `chapter2.md` | 1 |
> | `chapter3.md` | 4 |
> | `chapter4.md` | 6 |
> | `chapter5.md` | 5 |
> | `chapter6.md` | 2 |


# Expected behavior

LLM reports something like

> | Chapter | Content number |
> |---------|----------------|
> | `chapter1.md` | 1 |
> | `chapter2.md` | 2 |
> | `chapter3.md` | 3 |
> | `chapter4.md` | 4 |
> | `chapter5.md` | 5 |
> | `chapter6.md` | 6 |


# Log

I have used Zed's `Open Thread as Markdown` button to generate a log of what's happening: 
[2026-09-27_tool_call_test_report.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32696427/2026-09-27_tool_call_test_report.md)

As you can see, in the log it appears as if the correct content is sent to the LLM, but the LLM reports back something else.

### Reproduction steps

1. On Windows 11, enable the Microsoft IME (Japanese) with predictive input on (the default).
2. Open Zed's terminal panel docked at the bottom, so the input line sits near the bottom edge of the screen.
3. Start typing Japanese in the terminal, e.g. at the shell prompt or in a TUI such as Claude Code.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** There is not enough room below the input line, so the IME flips the candidate/prediction window above the caret. The bottom edge of that window then lands on the **vertical middle of the input line**, and it covers the upper half of the composition text. You can't see what you are typing while composing.

**Expected:** When the window flips above, its bottom edge should sit at the top of the input line, so the composition text stays visible.

**Likely cause:** On Windows the IME is given a single point instead of the caret rectangle, and that point is the vertical middle of the line:

- [`retrieve_caret_position`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/1a28cff4b409169bac058bca40dfbfeb7621d19b/crates/gpui_windows/src/events.rs#L650-L661) returns `y = origin.y + height / 2`.
- [`update_ime_position`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/1a28cff4b409169bac058bca40dfbfeb7621d19b/crates/gpui_windows/src/events.rs#L686-L693) passes that point to `ImmSetCandidateWindow` with `CFS_CANDIDATEPOS`, which carries no area to avoid.

When there's no space below, the IME can only place the window relative to that point, so it overlaps the line. Passing the full caret bounds (which `bounds_for_range` already returns: cursor cell × `line_height` in the terminal) as an exclusion area should fix it. That means `CFS_EXCLUDE` with `rcArea` set to the caret rect and `ptCurrentPos` at its bottom-left, so the IME can flip above the line instead of onto it.

The editor (same Windows code path) also misplaces the window, and the error changes with where on screen you type:

- **Typing near the bottom of the editor:** the window opens *below* the line, but several lines away from it, leaving a gap.
- **Typing near the top of the editor:** the window covers the composition text, as it does in the terminal.

The terminal case lines up with the single mid-line point described above. I haven't tracked down why the editor offset varies with vertical position.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: 1.21.0 (stable, 33c9585)
OS: Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200
Display: 1536×864 logical, 125% scaling
IME: Microsoft IME (Japanese)
Project opened via WSL remote (Ubuntu); the terminal is the remote shell.

### Relevant Zed settings

<details><summary>settings.json (terminal)</summary>

"terminal": {
  "font_family": "FiraCode Nerd Font Mono",

  "font_fallbacks": ["BIZ UDGothic"],
  "font_size": 15.6,
  "line_height": { "custom": 1.23 }
},
"text_rendering_mode": "grayscale"
```

</details>

Ubuntu

body_text:
### Summary

On Linux, the external Claude Agent (`claude-acp`) can sit on **"Authenticating to Claude Agent…"** indefinitely — in my case ~50 minutes across repeated attempts — with no timeout, no error, and no way to cancel from the UI. Same visible symptom as #53000 (closed `needs repro`); this report has the full causal chain from a Linux host.

The spinner is not an auth problem. It is the agent **reinstall** blocking underneath it. Three separate defects stack up:

---

### Defect 1 — Agent reinstall refetches every platform binary on each agent start (~268 MB)

`@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` pulls `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` plus **eight** platform packages. On my machine only one is usable, but six were present as **empty 4 KB stub directories**, so npm considered the tree incomplete and re-attempted them on every agent start:

```
223M  claude-agent-sdk-linux-x64        <- the only one this host can execute
 13M  claude-agent-sdk-linux-x64-musl   <- host is glibc 2.39, unusable
4.0K  claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64     <- empty stub, refetched every start
4.0K  claude-agent-sdk-darwin-x64       <- empty stub
4.0K  claude-agent-sdk-linux-arm64      <- empty stub
4.0K  claude-agent-sdk-linux-arm64-musl <- empty stub
4.0K  claude-agent-sdk-win32-arm64      <- empty stub
4.0K  claude-agent-sdk-win32-x64        <- empty stub
```

Zed's install does not constrain `--os` / `--cpu` / `--libc`, so a glibc x86-64 Linux host repeatedly downloads macOS, Windows and ARM binaries it can never run. On a fast link this is merely wasteful; on a slow or filtered link it is the difference between 17 seconds and never finishing.

**After** adding a directory-scoped `.npmrc` with `os=linux`, `cpu=x64`, `libc=glibc`, the same install completed in **17 seconds / `up to date`** instead of stalling for 9–15 minutes.

### Defect 2 — A killed or stalled install leaves a staging directory that permanently wedges every later install

body_text:
**What**: On 1.21 (Linux/NixOS, 15 GB RAM, 8 cores), launching with one large agent thread (4.4 MB stored, ~28 MB JSON) in the panel costs 30–60 s of input lag (terminal + chat), then smooths out.

**Measured A/B** — same build, same workspace, only the panel's thread differs (numbers from Zed's own `gpui churn` lines + hang traces):

| first 90 s after launch | large thread restored | empty thread |
|---|---|---|
| hang detections | 12 (incl. all 8 workers flagged at +2 s) | 8 (routine only: extension-host wasm ×4, language-registry ×2, project-environment ×2, all ≤220 ms) |
| thread-parse errors | 35 | 0 |
| `language not found` (diff restore) | 33 | 0 |
| entities created in one 30 s window | **54,436** | **455** |
| `flush_effects` ≥1000/s | ~90 s | none |

Loading the same thread *on demand* after startup costs 14,406 entities, +511 MiB, and one 346 ms foreground hang (`agent_ui/conversation_view.rs:1107`).

**Read**: the startup cost is dominated by building the thread's view (tens of thousands of GPUI entities), not workspace/extension startup. Deferring conversation-history construction until the panel is actually visible (or restoring it progressively during idle) would likely remove most of the first-minute saturation. The diff-language race in the same restore path is a separate small bug (fixed by a local patch; happy to send as a PR).

Measured on a locally built 1.21; the A/B is same-binary, only the panel state differs. Full log excerpts and the census script available on request.

On Windows, check out a branch in a worktree with a long path: `git worktree add C:/Users/me/Documents/a-fairly-long-repository-name/.worktrees/feature-branch feature-branch` 2. Open the main checkout in Zed. 3. In the branch picker, select `feature-branch`. ### Current vs. Expected behavior Current: the "Failed to change branch" dialog truncates the worktree path (`'C:/Users/me/Documents/a-fairly-long-repository-na…'`), which is exactly the part needed to act on the error. Expected: the full message is readable. [`prompt()`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/447f72e5167eb8ccc9dbbef9d3e9c96304867599/crates/gpui_windows/src/window.rs#L718-L793) uses a native TaskDialog, which wraps only at whitespace and ellipsizes any word wider than the dialog. Any prompt containing a long path is affected, not just Git ones. Tried in a standalone repro with the same TaskDialog config: - `TDF_SIZE_TO_CONTENT`: the dialog widens, but the path is still cut. - U+200B after `/` and `\`: the path wraps, but the invisible characters leak into Ctrl+C copies. Workaround: Ctrl+C on the dialog copies the full text. ### Zed version and system specs Zed: v1.21.0 (33c95853ed2b6956f339733c63a8220964ecbeb6) OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100 Architecture: x86_64 ### Attach Zed log file ### Relevant Zed settings ### Relevant Keymap ### (for AI issues) Model provider details _No response_ ### If you are using WSL on Windows, what flavor of Linux are you using? body_text:
### What happens

Threads created in a remote (SSH) project can end up with `remote_connection = NULL` in `sidebar_threads`. The sidebar only surfaces a thread under a remote project group when the thread's stored connection matches that project's host (`entries_for_main_worktree_path` / `entries_for_path` + `matches_remote_connection`), so those threads can never appear under their remote project — they only re-form a phantom *local* project group with the same paths. There is no in-product way to fix the association afterwards.

### Why it happens (as best we can tell from 1.21.0 / main)

The backfill `migrate_thread_remote_connections` fills missing connections by matching a thread's `folder_paths` / `main_worktree_paths` **exactly** against "recent remote workspaces that don't also exist as local workspaces", and it runs **once** (kv key `thread-metadata-remote-connection-backfill`):

- Path lists that don't line up exactly (linked worktrees, subfolders, any drift) are missed forever.
- If the path list also exists as a local workspace (common: same repo checked out on both sides), the remote entry is skipped by design, so threads that only ever lived remotely can still miss the tag.
- Once the key is set nothing re-runs or retries, and no UI action can re-associate a thread.

### Our data point

30 threads belonging to a remote `~/Company` (SSH) project: only 6 had a connection in `sidebar_threads`; 24 were `NULL` and invisible under the remote project group. We repaired them by writing the connection JSON directly into `sidebar_threads` — not something a user can do.

### Possible directions

- Set `remote_connection` when a thread is created/opened while the active workspace is remote (instead of relying only on a backfill).
- Make the backfill retryable / re-runnable when workspaces change, and match by most-specific path prefix instead of exact `PathList` equality.
- Give the user a way to re-associate a thread with a project/host once it's been mis-layered.

30 threads belonging to a remote `~/Company` (SSH) project: only 6 had a connection in `sidebar_threads`; 24 were `NULL` and invisible under the remote project group. We repaired them by writing the connection JSON directly into `sidebar_threads` — not something a user can do.

### Possible directions

- Set `remote_connection` when a thread is created/opened while the active workspace is remote (instead of relying only on a backfill).
- Make the backfill retryable / re-runnable when workspaces change, and match by most-specific path prefix instead of exact `PathList` equality.
- Give the user a way to re-associate a thread with a project/host once it's been mis-layered.

### What happens

With a remote (SSH) workspace waiting on a password prompt (the `zed --askpass` helper alive), the Zed UI thread spins at ~100% of a core. Measured over a 20 s window with per-thread CPU sampling: 99.8% of one core on the main thread; the same build idles at ~2% when no prompt is pending.

### Reproduction

1. Open a remote project over SSH with password auth (no key configured).
2. Leave the password prompt unanswered — keep using the local editor.
3. The main thread pegs (~100%), and the editor feels heavy for everything else.

### Workaround

Killing the stuck `ssh -N …ControlMaster=yes` process and its `zed --askpass` child drops the UI thread immediately (99.8% → ~13% in our measurement; it does not respawn).

### Notes

- Seen on 1.21.0, Linux/Wayland (also observed earlier on 1.20.1).
- `Zed.log` shows nothing recurring while it spins; it's userspace CPU on the main thread, not I/O.
- Happy to run more instrumentation (hang traces / stacks) if that would help.

body_text:
This appears to be caused by my having a banner/MOTD printed when `$nu.is-interactive` is true. Removing that behavior causes Zed to retrieve the shell environment without issue. Reading through `util::shell_env::capture_unix` this would be because zed passes `zed --printenv` into nushell via `-e` instead of `-c`. This is not correct: `-e` will execute in an interactive environment, where `-c` will not. That behavior is [explicitly written into nushell](https://github.com/nushell/nushell/blob/2459fdd134ea4fdbae42efd6924e2b41201cf363/src/main.rs#L309) and can not be circumvented - there is no more nuanced manner of setting `is-interactive`.

I suppose I can maybe work around this on my end by checking the tty, but the broader issue is that where it might make sense to use an interactive shell for this purpose with more traditional POSIX-style setups that do not evaluate certain files unless run interactively (or at least that is what the profile is written to do), I am not aware of any such convention existing for nushell, and it would make more sense to invoke with `-c` for a noninteractive session and see no reason to treat the exceptional case as the default when Zed should instead expect failures in the exceptional case to require correction on the part of the operator - not the other way around. Additionally, zed did not print an error indicating that it could not parse the output, even though that certainly appears to be what was happening.

I see that there is a comment to the effect of "Nushell does not allow for non-interactive login shells." If this was true, it no longer is:

```
> env -i nu -l -c 'zed --printenv'
{
  ...
}
```

The "bad" command cited in that comment is `nushell -l -i -c 'zed --printenv'` which specifies an *interactive login shell*, not a non-interactive login shell. Nonetheless, the comment is still wrong:

```
> env -i nu -l -i -c '$nu.is-interactive' 
true
> env -i nu -l -c '$nu.is-interactive' 
false
```

### Reproduction steps

1. Have a nushell configuration which displays a banner or similar when `$nu.is-interactive`
2. Observe that the effective `PATH` logged by `project::environment::local_directory_environment` is an empty string 

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior: zed fails to retrieve PATH and other environment variables, but does not produce an error
Expected behavior: zed retrieves PATH and other environment variables

{"repository": "zed-industries/zed", "task_candidate_id": 26889, "repository_id": 319, "issue_number": 64913, "github_issue_id": 5625190496, "html_url": "https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/64913", "created_at": "2026-09-29T04:38:54+00:00", "author_association": null, "title": "Shell environment capture uses Nushell’s interactive `-e` mode", "body_text": "This appears to be caused by my having a banner/MOTD printed when `$nu.is-interactive` is true. Removing that behavior causes Zed to retrieve the shell environment without issue. Reading through `util::shell_env::capture_unix` this would be because zed passes `zed --printenv` into nushell via `-e` instead of `-c`. This is not correct: `-e` will execute in an interactive environment, where `-c` will not. That behavior is [explicitly written into nushell](https://github.com/nushell/nushell/blob/2459fdd134ea4fdbae42efd6924e2b41201cf363/src/main.rs#L309) and can not be circumvented - there is no more nuanced manner of setting `is-interactive`.

I suppose I can maybe work around this on my end by checking the tty, but the broader issue is that where it might make sense to use an interactive shell for this purpose with more traditional POSIX-style setups that do not evaluate certain files unless run interactively (or at least that is what the profile is written to do), I am not aware of any such convention existing for nushell, and it would make more sense to invoke with `-c` for a noninteractive session and see no reason to treat the exceptional case as the default when Zed should instead expect failures in the exceptional case to require correction on the part of the operator - not the other way around. Additionally, zed did not print an error indicating that it could not parse the output, even though that certainly appears to be what was happening.

I see that there is a comment to the effect of "Nushell does not allow for non-interactive login shells." If this was true, it no longer is:

```
> env -i nu -l -c 'zed --printenv'
{
  ...
}
```

The "bad" command cited in that comment is `nushell -l -i -c 'zed --printenv'` which specifies an *interactive login shell*, not a non-interactive login shell. Nonetheless, the comment is still wrong:

```
> env -i nu -l -i -c '$nu.is-interactive' 
true
> env -i nu -l -c '$nu.is-interactive' 
false
```

### Reproduction steps

1. Have a nushell configuration which displays a banner or similar when `$nu.is-interactive`
2. Observe that the effective `PATH` logged by `project::environment::local_directory_environment` is an empty string 

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior: zed fails to retrieve PATH and other environment variables, but does not produce an error
Expected behavior: zed retrieves PATH and other environment variables

### Reproduction steps

1. Use the default buffer font, with ligatures enabled (the default).
2. Open a Python file and type:
```python
class Foo:
    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        pass

```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected behavior**
All of `__post_init__` uses the function name color, and only `(` uses the bracket color.

**Actual behavior**
The trailing `__` is drawn in the bracket color (`#0090FF` with `colorize_brackets` on).
`dev: open highlights tree view` shows the correct colors for each part, so the error happens when the text is drawn.

### Reproduction steps

1. Start a conversation with the built-in Zed Agent.
2. Ask the main agent to change File A. Open File A and confirm that the inline diff and Keep/Reject controls appear.
3. Ask the main agent to delegate a change to File B to a subagent.
4. Check both files: inline review has disappeared from File A but remains visible in File B.
5. Ask the main agent to change File A again. Its inline review still does not appear.

Keep the main conversation selected and leave all changes pending throughout.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** File A loses its inline diff and Keep/Reject controls after the subagent edits File B. Further main-agent edits do not restore them. The main chat still offers Keep/Reject for the pending changes.

**Expected:** Changes from both the main agent and its subagents remain reviewable inline.

> **Investigation and local fix (AI-assisted):** Starting a subagent appears to [switch inline review away from the main conversation](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/76659a55a8c10ed355a070f8764a0b1733e3c115/crates/agent_ui/src/conversation_view.rs#L1340). We changed this locally so review stays attached to the main conversation. Repeating the steps above then kept inline review working for both files, including the Keep/Reject buttons.

### Zed version and system specs

```text
Zed: 1.22.0 (stable)
OS: macOS 26.7 (25G229)
```

### Reproduction steps

1. Start zed, open a worktree with a file type that does something observable on LSP didSave.
2. Go to definition, causing you to end up in another worktree.
3. Save the file in the other worktree, observe that didSave gets emitted.
4. Quit zed.
5. Restore zed, save the file in the other worktree that got restored, observe that didSave never gets emitted.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

LSP didSave should fire when connected to a LSP and saving a file.

### Zed version and system specs

Reproduces on latest main branch. I'm on macos aarch64.
