{"repository": "zed-industries/zed", "task_candidate_id": 27072, "repository_id": 319, "issue_number": 65567, "github_issue_id": 5840895236, "html_url": "https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/65567", "created_at": "2026-10-14T02:29:11+00:00", "author_association": null, "title": "`readonly` (and other options) in `mounts` are silently dropped, so read-only bind mounts become writable", "body_text": "### Reproduction steps

1. Create a project with this `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`:

   {
     "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:bookworm",
     "mounts": [
       "source=${localWorkspaceFolder}/.devcontainer,target=${localWorkspaceFolder}/.devcontainer,type=bind,readonly"
     ]
   }

2. Open the project in Zed and choose "Open in Container".
3. In Zed's terminal, run:
   touch .devcontainer/x; echo "exit: $?"
   mount | grep .devcontainer

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: `touch` succeeds (exit 0), the file appears on the host, and `mount` shows the bind mount as `rw`. No warning is shown.

Expected: the mount is read-only, as with the official devcontainers/cli and VS Code: `touch` fails with "Read-only file system" and `mount` shows `ro`.

Cause: `MountDefinition` only has `source`, `target` and `type` (devcontainer_json.rs L69-L97, which also always appends `consistency=cached`). Both string parsers keep only those keys and skip everything else: `deserialize_mount_definition` (devcontainer_json.rs L512-L521, `// Ignore unknown keys`) and `parse_mount_definition_string` (devcontainer_manifest.rs L3333-L3355). A bare `readonly` flag has no `=`, so it is skipped too. `ro`, `readonly=true` and other Docker mount options are lost the same way.

https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/18787a9a080cf36b83dd342b0fe3c103371fa348/crates/dev_container/src/devcontainer_json.rs#L69-L97
https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/18787a9a080cf36b83dd342b0fe3c103371fa348/crates/dev_container/src/devcontainer_json.rs#L512-L521
https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/18787a9a080cf36b83dd342b0fe3c103371fa348/crates/dev_container/src/devcontainer_manifest.rs#L3333-L3355

This is security-relevant: read-only mounts are commonly used to protect host-side files (e.g. .git/hooks, .git/config) from processes in the container, and Zed silently makes them writable. Preserving the remaining options and passing them through to `--mount` would fix it. Present in 1.23.3 and main.

### Zed version and system specs

exit: 0

mac on /Users/<user>/Developer/zed-test-2 type virtiofs (rw,relatime)
mac on /Users/<user>/Developer/zed-test-2/.devcontainer type virtiofs (rw,relatime)
mac on /Users/<user>/Developer/zed-test-2/.git/config type virtiofs (rw,relatime)
mac on /Users/<user>/Developer/zed-test-2/.git/hooks type virtiofs (rw,relatime)
```

All three bind mounts were declared with `readonly` in devcontainer.json and all show `rw`. Zed's log shows no error or warning. Runtime: OrbStack 2.2.3, Docker 29.4.0.

### Reproduction steps

First of all, I only attempted to reproduce this on Windwos, I don't know if this also happens on other OS's

1. open the terminal tab
2. hit Enter a couple of times until you get a scroll bar (the buffer doesn't fit the terminal tab)
3. scroll up by a single mouse wheel notch/tick
4. verify that less then a second later the terminal scroll jumps a couple of pixels

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Hi!

Here is a video showcasing the issue:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f433f67d-0fe3-4a04-8acf-6421def9d295

I tried in both Powershell and CMD, and both had the same issue.
This only happens when scrolling down to the very bottom of the buffer or up from the bottom of the buffer, scrolling in the middle of the buffer doesn't trigger this jump.
Dragging the scroll bar (not using the mouse wheal) also triggers the jump when scrolling from and to the end of the buffer.

Scrolling to or from the top of the buffer also does not have this issue, only the bottom.

Once again, I only tested on Windows, not sure if this happen on macOS or Linux.

This is just a visual annoyance.

Thank you!

### Reproduction steps

1. Build up one very long thread whose tool outputs are large (file reads, diffs, build logs) until the stored row is tens of MiB compressed.
2. Leave that thread as the last active one, so the agent panel restores it at startup and keeps it loaded.
3. Scroll the thread / leave it open for a while.
4. Watch zed: open log — [zed::reliability] memory usage — and Task Manager → Details → Commit size for the Zed process.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

On Windows, with one long agent thread left as the last active thread, Zed's commit/virtual memory grows monotonically for the whole session and never comes back down, while resident stays comparatively small and oscillates in a ~500 MiB sawtooth every 30–60 s. A single Zed process reached 25 GiB of virtual memory (Task Manager "Commit size") with only 2.4–3.4 GiB resident after ~14 h of session, and Zed recorded hang traces during it.

The sawtooth period and amplitude match the size of the active thread, which points at the thread persistence path: save_thread_sync serializes the entire thread to a JSON String and then zstd-compresses it into a second full buffer on every save, and DbThread includes UI-only fields (ui_scroll_position, draft_prompt), so simply scrolling the panel re-triggers the whole serialize+compress cycle.

Root cause (code references, main today, same shape in v1.23.3)
crates/agent/src/thread_store.rs — the whole thread is handed over on save:

rust


pub fn save_thread(
    &mut self,
    id: acp::SessionId,
    thread: crate::DbThread,
    folder_paths: PathList,
    cx: &mut Context<Self>,
) -> Task<Result<()>> { /* ... */ database.save_thread(id, thread, folder_paths).await /* ... */ }
crates/agent/src/db.rs — save_thread_sync materializes two full-size copies of the thread on every save:

rust


let json_data = serde_json::to_string(&SerializedThread { thread, version: DbThread::VERSION })?;   // copy #1 (≈ thread size)
let connection = connection.lock();
let compressed = zstd::encode_all(json_data.as_bytes(), COMPRESSION_LEVEL)?;                        // copy #2 (compressed)
let data = compressed;
// ... INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET data = excluded.data
crates/agent/src/db.rs — DbThread carries UI state, so UI-only changes dirty the whole payload:

rust


pub draft_prompt: Option<Vec<acp_v2::ContentBlock>>,
pub ui_scroll_position: Option<SerializedScrollPosition>,
Notes:

For a 600 MiB thread, one save allocates ~600 MiB (JSON string) plus the compressed buffer while the previous serialized form is still alive — hence the sawtooth and, presumably, allocator arenas that are never returned to the OS (hence one-way commit growth).
load_thread likewise materializes the whole thread (zstd::decode_all + serde_json::from_slice into Vec<Arc<DbMessage>>), so a huge thread also pins hundreds of MiB for as long as it is open.
There is no size guard, pagination or dedup of writes; the test-only write_gate comment in db.rs even notes that in production "new save requests routinely arrive mid-write".
Related, but orthogonal: PR #63053 (coalesce thread saves) reduces the frequency; the double full-size allocation per save remains.
Suggested fixes
Serialize without the extra full-size String: serde_json::to_writer(&mut Vec<u8>, ...) (or to_vec), or reuse a scratch buffer across saves.
Compress with a streaming encoder (zstd::stream::Encoder over a Vec<u8>, or reuse a buffer) so the JSON copy and the compressed copy don't have to be alive simultaneously.
Don't persist UI-only state as part of the whole thread: write ui_scroll_position / draft_prompt into a small separate row or kv_store, or debounce and skip saves when only those fields changed.
Coalesce saves per thread (single in-flight save; latest-wins) — #63053.
Longer term: paginate messages instead of one monolithic JSON blob per thread, so opening a long thread doesn't require decoding everything and saving it doesn't require re-encoding everything.
User-side workarounds
/compact (or agent.auto_compact) keeps a thread's context small, but it does not by itself remove a giant payload that already exists.
Export and remove the giant threads: agent: open active thread as markdown, then delete/archive the thread. Archiving in the sidebar alone does not reclaim the payload.
Do not leave a huge thread as the last active one; restart Zed after long sessions to release the commit.
If a model's context window is smaller than 80k tokens, auto-compaction cannot run at all and Zed only offers "New From Summary" / "Start New Thread".

### Zed version and system specs

Zed 1.23.3 stable, Windows 11 x64, 24 logical CPUs / 32 GiB RAM.
Profile migrated from another machine, so threads.db contains a few large threads: 101 threads in total, 177 MiB compressed, of which four are 63.7 / 44.4 / 38.6 / 20.2 MiB (94 % of the database payload in 4 threads).
The active thread (the one restored as "last active") is the 44.4 MiB one, ≈600 MiB after zstd decompression, and it grew by 10 MiB during that session.

<details><summary>Zed.log</summary>

Log (Zed.log), 661 samples over the session:

Code block

...
2026-10-15T07:13:51  INFO [zed::reliability] memory usage: resident 2943 MiB (+602 MiB), virtual 25391 MiB
2026-10-15T07:14:51  INFO [zed::reliability] memory usage: resident 2431 MiB (-512 MiB), virtual 24436 MiB
2026-10-15T07:16:22  INFO [zed::reliability] memory usage: resident 2886 MiB (+454 MiB), virtual 25981 MiB
2026-10-15T07:18:22  INFO [zed::reliability] memory usage: resident 2987 MiB (+551 MiB), virtual 25562 MiB
...
2026-10-15T07:35:52  INFO [zed::reliability] memory usage: resident 2548 MiB (-424 MiB), virtual 24979 MiB
Observations:

</details>

resident is bounded (~1.2–3.4 GiB) and shows a clean ±450–650 MiB sawtooth whose amplitude tracks the active thread's decompressed size.

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed with default settings (`disable_ai: false`).
2. Open several projects in the same window (e.g. `File > Open Recent` → Enter, or `zed ~/project-a` then `zed ~/project-b`). In my case there were 10 projects in one window.
3. Open the project picker (`projects: open recent`) and confirm all projects are listed under the "This Window" header.
4. Open Settings → AI and turn on **Disable AI** (equivalent to `"disable_ai": true` in settings.json).
5. Open the project picker again.

reduced repro with 2 projects attached

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a74e695f-2526-4dca-9782-d50fa7dc46ad

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior**

- Immediately after step 4, every project in the window except the currently active one is closed. There is no confirmation, no notification, and no undo. With 10 projects open, 9 were dropped.
- The "This Window" section no longer appears in the project picker. Selecting a recent project now replaces the current one instead of switching between projects held in the window.
- `multi_workspace::NextWorkspace` / `PreviousWorkspace` and the workspace sidebar stop working.

### Summary

When using the **Google Antigravity** (`antigravity-acp`) external agent in Zed's Agent Panel, the composer frequently gets permanently stuck showing the rotating blue `IconName::LoadCircle` spinner (`"Loading Added Context…"`) in the bottom-right corner where the Send/Stop button normally is. Once in this state, pressing `Enter` or attempting to send any new message in that thread is silently ignored.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an **Antigravity** (`antigravity-acp`) thread in the Agent Panel and send a prompt.
2. While a turn is running (or when `antigravity-acp` stalls on a turn/tool call or model rebuild), either:
   - Queue a follow-up message and trigger "Send Now" / fast-track `Enter` on an empty composer (`ThreadView::dispatch_queued_entry`), or
   - Interrupt/cancel a turn and send a follow-up prompt before the ACP server finishes unwinding the previous `session/prompt` RPC.
3. Observe that the thread's foreground state transitions to `Idle` (the Stop button disappears), the composer is emptied, and the bottom-right button becomes a spinning blue circle (`IconName::LoadCircle`).
4. Type a new message and press `Enter`: nothing happens; new messages cannot be sent in the thread.

### Root Cause Analysis

This is caused by an interaction between `ThreadView::dispatch_queued_entry` / `ThreadView::send_content` in `crates/agent_ui/src/conversation_view/thread_view.rs`, `AcpThread::cancel_inner` in `crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs`, and `antigravity-acp`'s handling of `session/cancel`:

1. **Why the spinner renders and blocks all sends (`crates/agent_ui/src/conversation_view/thread_view.rs`)**:
   - In `ThreadView::render_send_button`, the rotating blue accent spinner (`Icon::new(IconName::LoadCircle).color(Color::Accent).with_rotate_animation(3)`) is rendered whenever `self.is_loading_contents == true`.
   - While `self.is_loading_contents == true`, `ThreadView::send`, `ThreadView::interrupt_and_send`, and `ThreadView::regenerate` all return early (`if self.is_loading_contents { return; }`), preventing any further messages from being sent.

2. **Why `self.is_loading_contents` stays `true` forever (`thread_view.rs` + `acp_thread.rs`)**:
   - In `ThreadView::dispatch_queued_entry`:
     ```rust
     let cancelled = self.thread.update(cx, |thread, cx| thread.cancel(cx));
     ...
     let contents_task = cx.spawn_in(window, async move |_this, cx| {
         cancelled.await;
         ...
         Ok(Some((content, tracked_buffers)))
     });
     self.send_content(contents_task, is_native_command, window, cx);
     ```
   - `ThreadView::send_content` immediately sets `self.is_loading_contents = true` and creates a `guard = cx.new(|_| ())` whose `on_release` callback resets `this.is_loading_contents = false`.
   - `guard` is moved into the spawned task and is only dropped **after** `contents_task.await` completes.
   - `contents_task` awaits `cancelled.await`, which comes from `AcpThread::cancel_inner` (`crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs`):
     ```rust
     if let Some(turn) = self.running_turn.take() {
         ...
         self.set_foreground_state(StateUpdate::Idle, cx);
         cx.background_spawn(async move {
             let _ = cancel_task.await;
             let _ = turn.send_task.await;
         })
     }
     ```
   - Notice that `AcpThread::cancel_inner` **immediately** sets `foreground_state` to `Idle` (so the UI no longer shows a running turn or Stop button), while `cancelled.await` blocks on `turn.send_task.await` (waiting for the ACP server to resolve the cancelled in-flight `session/prompt` JSON-RPC request).
   - If the ACP server does not promptly return a response to the cancelled `session/prompt` RPC, `turn.send_task.await` never resolves -> `cancelled.await` never resolves -> `contents_task.await` never resolves -> `guard` is never dropped -> `self.is_loading_contents` remains `true` permanently.

3. **Why `antigravity-acp` (`v1.4.0`) does not resolve `session/prompt` on `session/cancel`**:
   - In `antigravity-acp` (`server.py` / `local_connection.py`), `prompt()` iterates `async for step in agent.conversation.receive_steps():`, which awaits `self._processor.step_queue.get()` until `localharness_external` emits a WebSocket `TrajectoryStateUpdate` with `STATE_FULLY_IDLE` or `STATE_CANCELLED` (`IDLE_SENTINEL`).
   - `cancel()` sends `InputEvent(halt_request=True)` over stdin to `localharness_external`, but does not wake or time out `step_queue.get()`. If `localharness_external` does not emit `STATE_CANCELLED`/`STATE_FULLY_IDLE` (for example after a CCPA proxy timeout, a hung tool step, or when a second turn triggers `wait_for_idle()` on a concurrent `receive_steps()`), the `session/prompt` RPC hangs indefinitely.

### Zed Version and System Specs

- **Zed**: `v1.24.2`
- **External Agent**: `antigravity-acp` `v_1.4.0_74b860b327066613_e85154aa2cb85b9a`
- **OS**: macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)

   - While `self.is_loading_contents == true`, `ThreadView::send`, `ThreadView::interrupt_and_send`, and `ThreadView::regenerate` all return early (`if self.is_loading_contents { return; }`), preventing any further messages from being sent.

2. **Why `self.is_loading_contents` stays `true` forever (`thread_view.rs` + `acp_thread.rs`)**:
   - In `ThreadView::dispatch_queued_entry`:
     ```rust
     let cancelled = self.thread.update(cx, |thread, cx| thread.cancel(cx));
     ...
     let contents_task = cx.spawn_in(window, async move |_this, cx| {
         cancelled.await;
         ...
         Ok(Some((content, tracked_buffers)))
     });
     self.send_content(contents_task, is_native_command, window, cx);
     ```
   - `ThreadView::send_content` immediately sets `self.is_loading_contents = true` and creates a `guard = cx.new(|_| ())` whose `on_release` callback resets `this.is_loading_contents = false`.
   - `guard` is moved into the spawned task and is only dropped **after** `contents_task.await` completes.
   - `contents_task` awaits `cancelled.await`, which comes from `AcpThread::cancel_inner` (`crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs`):
     ```rust
     if let Some(turn) = self.running_turn.take() {
         ...
         self.set_foreground_state(StateUpdate::Idle, cx);
         cx.background_spawn(async move {
             let _ = cancel_task.await;
             let _ = turn.send_task.await;
         })
     }
     ```
   - Notice that `AcpThread::cancel_inner` **immediately** sets `foreground_state` to `Idle` (so the UI no longer shows a running turn or Stop button), while `cancelled.await` blocks on `turn.send_task.await` (waiting for the ACP server to resolve the cancelled in-flight `session/prompt` JSON-RPC request).
   - If the ACP server does not promptly return a response to the cancelled `session/prompt` RPC, `turn.send_task.await` never resolves -> `cancelled.await` never resolves -> `contents_task.await` never resolves -> `guard` is never dropped -> `self.is_loading_contents` remains `true` permanently.

3. **Why `antigravity-acp` (`v1.4.0`) does not resolve `session/prompt` on `session/cancel`**:
   - In `antigravity-acp` (`server.py` / `local_connection.py`), `prompt()` iterates `async for step in agent.conversation.receive_steps():`, which awaits `self._processor.step_queue.get()` until `localharness_external` emits a WebSocket `TrajectoryStateUpdate` with `STATE_FULLY_IDLE` or `STATE_CANCELLED` (`IDLE_SENTINEL`).
   - `cancel()` sends `InputEvent(halt_request=True)` over stdin to `localharness_external`, but does not wake or time out `step_queue.get()`. If `localharness_external` does not emit `STATE_CANCELLED`/`STATE_FULLY_IDLE` (for example after a CCPA proxy timeout, a hung tool step, or when a second turn triggers `wait_for_idle()` on a concurrent `receive_steps()`), the `session/prompt` RPC hangs indefinitely.

### Zed Version and System Specs

- **Zed**: `v1.24.2`

### Reproduction steps

I found this in DBFlux, a GPUI app built on `gpui-pre` 0.3.9 (a snapshot of `zed@93d7456`), and have not reproduced it in Zed itself. The code involved is unchanged on Zed's `main` (`4a8ccb3`), so Zed should hit it the same way.

1. On a Wayland session (Hyprland 0.56.2 here), run fcitx5 as the input method (`XMODIFIERS=@im=fcitx`) with a US layout.
2. Give a text input focus, so fcitx5 relays keys through its virtual keyboard.
3. Hold Ctrl+Shift and press a key binding that moves focus out of the text input.
4. Still holding Ctrl+Shift, or pressing them again, press a binding on a shifted digit or symbol, for example `ctrl-^` (Ctrl+Shift+6).

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior: the first key after focus leaves the text input arrives without its Shift level. Ctrl+Shift+6 arrives as `ctrl-6`, so a `ctrl-^` binding does not fire. The next press arrives as `ctrl-^`. Shift on a letter is not affected, because `keystroke_from_xkb` takes Shift from `state.modifiers` for letters.

Expected behavior: the key resolves with the modifiers that are held, on the first press.

Cause: on `wl_keyboard::Event::Keymap`, `crates/gpui_linux/src/linux/wayland/client.rs` replaces the state with `xkb::State::new(&keymap)`, which has no modifiers until the next `wl_keyboard::Event::Modifiers`. When focus leaves the text input, the compositor switches from fcitx5's virtual keyboard back to the physical keyboard. It sends the new keymap and then the next key, with no `Modifiers` event between them, so `key_get_one_sym` resolves the key at the base level. Raw events logged in the `wl_keyboard` handler, with Ctrl+Shift held (`depressed=5`):

```
keymap event (state being replaced had depressed=5 latched=0 locked=16)
key keysym=6                  -> "ctrl-6"
keymap event (state being replaced had depressed=0 latched=0 locked=0)
modifiers depressed=0 latched=0 locked=16
modifiers depressed=5 latched=0 locked=16
key keysym=asciicircum        -> "ctrl-^"
```

Carrying the previous state's modifier masks into the new state fixes it:

```rust
let mut keymap_state = xkb::State::new(&keymap);
if let Some(previous) = state.keymap_state.as_ref() {
    keymap_state.update_mask(
        previous.serialize_mods(xkb::STATE_MODS_DEPRESSED),
        previous.serialize_mods(xkb::STATE_MODS_LATCHED),
        previous.serialize_mods(xkb::STATE_MODS_LOCKED),
        0,
        0,
        previous.serialize_layout(xkb::STATE_LAYOUT_LOCKED),
    );
}
state.keymap_state = Some(keymap_state);
```

This copies the masks bit for bit, which assumes both keymaps order their modifiers the same way, as keymaps compiled from xkeyboard-config do. DBFlux carries this patch in its vendored copy of `gpui-pre-linux` (0xErwin1/dbflux#1078) with a unit test: a US keymap with Shift held, the state replaced, and `6` expected to resolve to `asciicircum`.

### Zed version and system specs

Not reproduced in Zed; found with `gpui-pre-linux` 0.3.9 (`zed@93d7456`), code unchanged on `main` at `4a8ccb3`.
OS: Arch Linux (Omarchy), Hyprland 0.56.2, fcitx5 5.1.22
Architecture: x86_64

### Summary

When an OpenAI-compatible provider returns a tool call with an **empty `id`** (and, in the case captured here, an empty `function.name` as well), Zed accumulates it as a normal tool call, executes it, and writes the exchange into the thread history. On the next turn Zed replays that history with the empty-string identity, and the provider rejects the request. Pressing **Retry** re-sends the identical messages, so the thread is permanently wedged.

Both variants reduce to the same root cause:

  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "\n\n",
  "tool_calls": [

      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "",
        "arguments": "{\"command\":\"<some shell command>\",\"cd\":\"/path/to/project\"}"
      }

  "reasoning_content": "..."

  "tool_call_id": ""

```rust

### Reproduction steps

In the worktree picker, to delete a worktree, you must first click the `x` next to it, then it moves down to the bottom of the list of worktrees. So you need to scroll down to the bottom of the list, find your worktree again, then click the trash icon next to it (where the x was before). 

### Current vs. Expected behavior

This used to be simple: before the worktree would stay in place, so a simple double-click would remove the worktree from the window _and_ delete it. Now that worktrees are grouped by "in window" and "not in window", this movement makes deleting worktrees difficult and unintuitive.

I would like to revert to that behavior, either by delaying the move to the "outside window" group by a split second (or better yet on mouse-out event of the worktree row) to allow me to click a second time or by adding configuration to remove the grouping entirely (and allow for sorting by recency).

I filed this as a bug rather than a feature request because it's a regression: double click used to work to delete a worktree.

### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed
2. Create a Python file with the following contents
```
import collections
import argparse
import math

def main():
    x = math.cos(2.0)
    y = collections.defaultdict(int)

    z = argparse.ArgumentParser()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
3. Repeatedly format the file (alt+shift+f) and undo (ctrl+z)

### Current vs. Expected behavior

#### Current behavior:
Occasionally, _the buffer's text is modified in meaningful ways_. I have seen lines both deleted and added. In this particular example, after a few cycles of formatting and undoing I got the buffer to become this (note the duplication of `z = argparse.ArgumentParser()`:

```
import argparse
import collections
import math


def main():
    x = math.cos(2.0)
    y = collections.defaultdict(int)

    z = argparse.ArgumentParser()

    z = argparse.ArgumentParser()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

I have also verified that this is a real textual change (the extra line appears in other editors) and not just a rendering bug.

#### Expected behavior:

Formatting only makes cosmetic changes to the program and never changes the meaning.

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

1. Create a git repo with a linked worktree:
   git init main && cd main && git commit --allow-empty -m init
   git worktree add ../wt-a
2. Open `wt-a` in Zed (`zed ../wt-a`).
3. In the Agent Panel, start one or two threads with an external ACP agent (I use `pi-acp` from the registry). They appear in the sidebar under the repo's group (e.g. "main").
4. `workspace: new file`, type some text, then `workspace: save as` to a path outside the project, e.g. `~/Desktop/questions.md`.
5. Look at the threads sidebar and the Agent Panel.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior:**

- The saved file becomes a visible project root. In `db/0-stable/db.sqlite`, the workspace row changes:
  - `paths`: `[…/wt-a, ~/Desktop/questions.md]` (`paths_order` `0,1`)
  - `identity_paths`: `[…/main, ~/Desktop/questions.md]`
- Every **non-archived** thread for that workspace has `folder_paths` and `main_worktree_paths` in `sidebar_threads` rewritten to include the file. Archived threads are left as they were.
- The sidebar moves those threads out of the "app-product" group into a new group, "app-product, questions.md".
- The Agent Panel warns: *"This agent doesn't currently support multi-root workspaces. It currently only operates by default on 'app-product'."*

*(attach both screenshots: sidebar + warning)*

**Expected behavior:** The saved file should open like any non-project file, the way opening an existing file outside the project does. The workspace roots, thread grouping and agent should stay as they were.

**Notes:**

- Opening an existing file outside the project (e.g. `/tmp/foo.md`) does **not** cause this. Only saving a new buffer there does.
- It happened twice, with different file types: 6 Oct with `~/Desktop/asdasdsadasda.json` and 15 Oct with `~/Desktop/questions.md`.
- Workaround: in the Project Panel, right-click the file's root and choose **Remove from Project**. The threads then move back to the original group.

body_text: Since #59839 moved branch/tag refs out of the Description column into a dedicated gutter to the left of the graph, the Git Graph has two usability regressions. ### Reproduction steps 1. Open a repository that has a few branches, including remote branches (e.g. `origin/`) and a checked-out local branch. 2. Open the Git Graph (`git graph: open`). 3. Look at the area to the left of the graph lanes. ### Current vs. Expected behavior **1. The ref gutter wastes a lot of horizontal space** `ref_label_gutter_width` computes a single width (clamped to `REF_LABEL_GUTTER_MIN_WIDTH = 240px` / `REF_LABEL_GUTTER_MAX_WIDTH = 280px`) and reserves it on **every** row as soon as the repository has at least one ref. In practice only a handful of commits near the top carry refs, so the vast majority of rows show ~240px of empty space to the left of the graph. There is no way to hide or shrink it. **2. Branch names are truncated, and the most important ones the worst** Because the gutter is capped at 280px, chips get ellipsized: - `origin/d…` — the `origin/` prefix consumes half the chip, so the actual branch name is not visible. - `HEAD → syh…` — the `HEAD →` prefix leaves only ~3 characters of the currently checked-out branch, which is the single most important ref in the graph. - `+1` — additional refs on the same commit collapse into a count chip and require a click to discover. **Expected:** refs should be readable without wasting space on rows that have no refs. Some possible directions: - A setting to choose the placement, e.g. `"git_graph": { "ref_labels": "gutter" | "description" }`, so users can go back to inline refs in the Description column. - Or only spend space where refs exist (e.g. render chips as an overlay / inline next to the commit node instead of reserving a fixed-width gutter on every row), and show the full ref name on hover. - Or at least make the gutter resizable/collapsible like the other table columns, and avoid truncating the `HEAD → ` chip first. ### Zed version and system specs Zed: v1.24.2 (build 20261014.161923) OS: macOS 26.6.2 Memory: 36 GiB Architecture: aarch64

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

1. Open a remote project over SSH. The SSH target is another user on the same machine (127.0.0.1).
2. The project's `.zed/tasks.json` is committed to the branch the worktree is created from. It has a task with `"hooks": ["create_worktree"]` (mine copies untracked files like `.env` from the main worktree and runs `npm install`).
3. Create a new worktree from the git worktree picker.
4. Zed opens the new worktree as a new workspace.

Related: #55714 (same symptom, but there the cause was an untracked `.zed`, which is not my case) and #63099 (same `GitWorktreeCreatedAt` log line, but in a devcontainer).

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: the hook does not run. Nothing changes in the new worktree, no terminal opens, and I get no error. `.zed/tasks.json` is present in the new worktree. If I open a file and start the same task from `task: spawn`, it works fine, so the task itself is OK. The log has no hook lines at all.

Expected: the `create_worktree` task runs after the worktree is created, like in a local project.

Other things I saw in the same flow:
- The new workspace opens with a reset window. The sidebars that were open in the previous workspace are closed.
- Creating the worktree prompted me for my git SSH key passphrase. I don't know if that is expected.
- The hooked task only shows in `task: spawn` when a file is open.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: v1.24.2+stable (Zed) 
OS: Linux Wayland arch
Memory: 62.3 GiB
Architecture: x86_64
GPU: Intel(R) Arc(tm) Graphics (MTL) || Intel open-source Mesa driver || Mesa 26.2.4-arch1.1

### Attach Zed log file

The only lines about worktrees, from the moment the worktree was created:

```
WARN  [git_ui_core::created_worktrees] Couldn't determine creation time for worktree .../worktrees/develop/grand-oak/develop; it won't be eligible for automatic archival: RPC request GitWorktreeCreatedAt failed: creation time unavailable for .../develop/.git/worktrees/develop: creation time is not available on this platform currently
ERROR [remote::remote_client] (remote server) server:error handling message. type:GitWorktreeCreatedAt, error:creation time unavailable for .../develop/.git/worktrees/develop: creation time is not available on this platform currently
```

The filesystem does report a birth time (`stat -c %w` on that path prints one), so this looks like it comes from the remote server side.

### Reproduction steps

1. On Windows, add a PATH entry with an unbalanced double quote before the Git directory. My Machine PATH had this, written by an installer:
   `...;C:\Program Files\Tailscale";C:\Program Files\Warp\bin;C:\Program Files\Git\cmd;...`
   `git` still works in PowerShell and cmd.
2. Start Zed and open a git repository that the current user owns.
3. Open the Git panel.
4. Click **Trust Directory**.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

### Summary

In Zed Preview 1.25.0 (macOS), Settings → AI → LLM Providers → OpenCode shows these errors even with a valid API key configured:

```
Failed to load OpenCode Zen models: missing field `npm`
Failed to load OpenCode Go models: missing field `npm`
```

Zed.log:

```
WARN [language_models::provider::opencode] Failed to fetch OpenCode Zen models: missing field `npm`
WARN [language_models::provider::opencode] Failed to fetch OpenCode Go models: missing field `npm`
```

No OpenCode models are listed as a result.

### Root cause

`crates/language_models/src/provider/opencode.rs` declares the per-model transport with a required `npm`:

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ModelTransport {
    npm: String,
}
```

But the catalog it fetches (`https://models.opencode.ai/api.json`) returns, for most models in `opencode` and `opencode-go`, a `provider` object with only `api` and no `npm`:

```json
"provider": { "api": "https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1" }
```

I checked the live catalog: dozens of models in both `opencode` and `opencode-go` have this shape (for example `glm-5`, `kimi-k2.5`, `deepseek-v4-pro`). The provider level still carries `"npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"`. `serde_json::from_value::<RichCatalogProvider>` fails on the first such model, so the whole catalog is rejected.

### Suggested fix

Make the field optional so the existing provider-level fallback in `parse_discovered_models` (`.or(provider.npm.as_deref())`) takes over:

```rust
struct ModelTransport {
    npm: Option<String>,
}
// ...
let transport = metadata
    .provider
    .as_ref()
    .and_then(|provider| provider.npm.as_deref())
    .or(provider.npm.as_deref());
```

The in-file test fixtures all include `npm`, so a fixture with `"provider": {"api": "..."}` would cover this.

### Environment

Zed Preview 1.25.0, macOS (Apple Silicon), OpenCode API key configured.

In Zed Preview 1.25.0 (macOS), Settings → AI → LLM Providers → OpenCode shows these errors even with a valid API key configured:

```
Failed to load OpenCode Zen models: missing field `npm`
Failed to load OpenCode Go models: missing field `npm`
```

Zed.log:

```
WARN [language_models::provider::opencode] Failed to fetch OpenCode Zen models: missing field `npm`
WARN [language_models::provider::opencode] Failed to fetch OpenCode Go models: missing field `npm`
```

No OpenCode models are listed as a result.

### Root cause

`crates/language_models/src/provider/opencode.rs` declares the per-model transport with a required `npm`:

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ModelTransport {
    npm: String,
}
```

But the catalog it fetches (`https://models.opencode.ai/api.json`) returns, for most models in `opencode` and `opencode-go`, a `provider` object with only `api` and no `npm`:

```json
"provider": { "api": "https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1" }
```

I checked the live catalog: dozens of models in both `opencode` and `opencode-go` have this shape (for example `glm-5`, `kimi-k2.5`, `deepseek-v4-pro`). The provider level still carries `"npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"`. `serde_json::from_value::<RichCatalogProvider>` fails on the first such model, so the whole catalog is rejected.

### Suggested fix

Make the field optional so the existing provider-level fallback in `parse_discovered_models` (`.or(provider.npm.as_deref())`) takes over:

```rust
struct ModelTransport {
    npm: Option<String>,
}
// ...
let transport = metadata
    .provider
    .as_ref()
    .and_then(|provider| provider.npm.as_deref())
    .or(provider.npm.as_deref());
```

The in-file test fixtures all include `npm`, so a fixture with `"provider": {"api": "..."}` would cover this.

My Goal:
Add a character between selections when there is no space between selection with helix keymap
Example: `noob` -> `"n""o""o""b"` or `123` -> `"1""2""3"`

### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed and open a .txt file
2. type a word in a line (example `noob`)
3. Try to add double quotes (or any character) around all characters in this word with helix keymap

    Steps:
      - select the whole line with `x`
      - search for individual characters in the word with `\w` and regex enabled (it also crashes if I search for individual characters)
      - Once all the characters are selected individually, add double quotes for all of them at the same time ( `noob` -> `"n""o""o""b"`)
      - App crashes

Extra info:
- It also happens when I try without regular expressions: converting `aaa` -> `"a""a""a"` by selecting the line, pressing `s` to search for `a` and having 3 different `a` selections 
- It also happens for multi character selections that have no space between them
- It also happens when when there is at least 2 adjacent selections without a space between them (converting `if  ifif` -> `"if"  "if""if"`)
- The same action works in helix editor.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed 1.24.2
Os: Windows 11

body_text:
## What I want

Let me pick the shell the Agent terminal tool uses on Windows. Right now it always picks Git Bash when Git-for-Windows is installed, with no setting to choose PowerShell instead.

## Current behavior

On Windows with Git-for-Windows installed, the Agent terminal tool runs under Git Bash (MINGW64/MSYS), even when my terminal panel is set to PowerShell.

Two call sites share that choice. A fix has to change both; editing only one leaves the other on Bash.

- Native agent tool: `crates/agent/src/tools/terminal_tool.rs` calls `AcpThread::create_terminal` in `crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs`, which uses `get_default_system_shell_preferring_bash()` and ignores `TerminalSettings` / `terminal.shell`.
- External ACP agents (`terminal/create`): `crates/agent_servers/src/acp/v1.rs` `handle_create_terminal` calls `create_terminal_entity` in `crates/acp_thread/src/terminal.rs`, which wraps the same helper in `Shell::Program(...)`.
- `crates/util/src/shell.rs` `get_default_system_shell_preferring_bash()` returns `get_windows_bash()` when `git-bash.exe` plus `bin/bash.exe` are found via `GIT_INSTALL_ROOT` or `which git`, else `get_windows_system_shell()`.
- `crates/gpui_util/src/lib.rs` `get_windows_system_shell()` prefers `pwsh.exe` / `powershell.exe`, falling back to `cmd.exe`.
- `crates/agent_settings/src/agent_settings.rs` has no shell option.

Launching an external agent is a different path. `crates/agent_servers/src/acp/transport.rs` `spawn_stdio` uses `Shell::System`, so the agent process itself starts under PowerShell. Only the terminal tool prefers Bash.

So `terminal.shell` in `settings.json` only affects the terminal panel, not the Agent tool. The only workaround is making bash undiscoverable (unset `GIT_INSTALL_ROOT`, hide `git-bash.exe`), then restart Zed to fall through to PowerShell.

## Expected behavior

Either:

- Respect the existing `terminal.shell` setting in the Agent terminal tool, or
- Add a dedicated `agent.shell` setting (e.g. `agent.terminal_shell`) with the same `Shell` enum (`system` / `program` / `with_arguments`).

Apply that choice in both `AcpThread::create_terminal` and `create_terminal_entity`.

## Why it matters

- PowerShell-native repos (modules, profiles, execution policy, PS-specific tooling) are awkward from Bash.
- External ACP agents send the raw command and let Zed's shell interpret it. Reproduced with Grok Build (`grok agent stdio`) on Zed Preview 1.25.0: the agent described the tool as PowerShell 7, and the process was Git Bash (`MINGW64`, `/usr/bin/bash`).
- Related but distinct from #55743 (MSYS2 stub `bash.exe` os error 193 plus invalid pwsh fallback syntax). This is a feature request for explicit shell choice, which would also sidestep that bug class.

## System

- OS: Windows 11
- Zed: stable (agent panel, native agent). Same behavior on Zed Preview 1.25.0 (`aa9c168`) with an external ACP agent.
- Git-for-Windows installed, so bash is auto-preferred today

{"repository": "zed-industries/zed", "task_candidate_id": 27111, "repository_id": 319, "issue_number": 65726, "github_issue_id": 5889838675, "html_url": "https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/65726", "created_at": "2026-10-16T19:15:45+00:00", "author_association": null, "title": "Agent terminal tool ignores terminal.shell, always prefers Git Bash on Windows - allow PowerShell", "body_text": "## What I want

Let me pick the shell the Agent terminal tool uses on Windows. Right now it always picks Git Bash when Git-for-Windows is installed, with no setting to choose PowerShell instead.

## Current behavior

On Windows with Git-for-Windows installed, the Agent terminal tool runs under Git Bash (MINGW64/MSYS), even when my terminal panel is set to PowerShell.

Two call sites share that choice. A fix has to change both; editing only one leaves the other on Bash.

- Native agent tool: `crates/agent/src/tools/terminal_tool.rs` calls `AcpThread::create_terminal` in `crates/acp_thread/src/acp_thread.rs`, which uses `get_default_system_shell_preferring_bash()` and ignores `TerminalSettings` / `terminal.shell`.
- External ACP agents (`terminal/create`): `crates/agent_servers/src/acp/v1.rs` `handle_create_terminal` calls `create_terminal_entity` in `crates/acp_thread/src/terminal.rs`, which wraps the same helper in `Shell::Program(...)`.
- `crates/util/src/shell.rs` `get_default_system_shell_preferring_bash()` returns `get_windows_bash()` when `git-bash.exe` plus `bin/bash.exe` are found via `GIT_INSTALL_ROOT` or `which git`, else `get_windows_system_shell()`.
- `crates/gpui_util/src/lib.rs` `get_windows_system_shell()` prefers `pwsh.exe` / `powershell.exe`, falling back to `cmd.exe`.
- `crates/agent_settings/src/agent_settings.rs` has no shell option.

Launching an external agent is a different path. `crates/agent_servers/src/acp/transport.rs` `spawn_stdio` uses `Shell::System`, so the agent process itself starts under PowerShell. Only the terminal tool prefers Bash.

So `terminal.shell` in `settings.json` only affects the terminal panel, not the Agent tool. The only workaround is making bash undiscoverable (unset `GIT_INSTALL_ROOT`, hide `git-bash.exe`), then restart Zed to fall through to PowerShell.

## Expected behavior

Either:

- Respect the existing `terminal.shell` setting in the Agent terminal tool, or
- Add a dedicated `agent.shell` setting (e.g. `agent.terminal_shell`) with the same `Shell` enum (`system` / `program` / `with_arguments`).

Apply that choice in both `AcpThread::create_terminal` and `create_terminal_entity`.

## Why it matters

- PowerShell-native repos (modules, profiles, execution policy, PS-specific tooling) are awkward from Bash.
- External ACP agents send the raw command and let Zed's shell interpret it. Reproduced with Grok Build (`grok agent stdio`) on Zed Preview 1.25.0: the agent described the tool as PowerShell 7, and the process was Git Bash (`MINGW64`, `/usr/bin/bash`).
- Related but distinct from #55743 (MSYS2 stub `bash.exe` os error 193 plus invalid pwsh fallback syntax). This is a feature request for explicit shell choice, which would also sidestep that bug class.

## System

- OS: Windows 11
- Zed: stable (agent panel, native agent). Same behavior on Zed Preview 1.25.0 (`aa9c168`) with an external ACP agent.
- Git-for-Windows installed, so bash is auto-preferred today

Co-Authored-By: Zed

This causes some noticeable bugs with semi-transparent themes. ## Example As shown below, the Git gutter colors are completely invisible with these settings: The Git gutter becomes visible only when it's fully opaque. This is caused by the above incorrect alpha compositing logic. ## Fix The fix actually requires very little code: ```rs impl Rgba { /// Create a new [`Rgba`] color by blending this and another color together pub fn blend(&self, other: Rgba) -> Self { if other.a >= 1.0 { other } else if other.a <= 0.0 { *self } else { let background_alpha = self.a * (1.0 - other.a); let alpha = other.a + background_alpha; Rgba { r: (self.r * background_alpha + other.r * other.a) / alpha, g: (self.g * background_alpha + other.g * other.a) / alpha, b: (self.b * background_alpha + other.b * other.a) / alpha, a: alpha, } } } ``` But any attempt to fix it will certainly be a BREAKING CHANGE! It may break many transparent themes that rely on the previous behavior! Still, I personally believe this issue should be fixed sooner rather than later. Zed v1.24.2

### Summary

On Windows, opening a project with a string-form `initializeCommand` always fails before the container is built. Since #60792, Zed wraps string-form lifecycle commands in `/bin/sh -c`. But `initializeCommand` runs on the **host**, and Windows has no `/bin/sh`, so `Command::new("/bin/sh")` fails with `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` (os error 3) and the container never starts.

### Reproduction steps

1. On Windows, create a project with `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:bookworm",
     "initializeCommand": "echo hello"
   }
   ```
2. Open the project in Zed and choose "Open in Container".

### Current behavior

Startup fails immediately, before any container work:

```
ERROR [dev_container::devcontainer_json] Error running command default: Das System kann den angegebenen Pfad nicht finden. (os error 3)
ERROR [recent_projects::remote_servers] Failed to start dev container: DevContainerUpFailed("Failed with nested error: CommandFailed(\"default\")")
```

("Das System kann den angegebenen Pfad nicht finden" is the German text for Win32 `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND` — the missing path is `/bin/sh`.)

### Expected behavior

`initializeCommand` runs on the host and the container starts, matching the official devcontainers/cli and VS Code on Windows.

### Cause

`crates/dev_container/src/devcontainer_json.rs`, `LifecycleScript::from_str` -> `shell_command`:

```rust
fn shell_command(script: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    vec!["/bin/sh".to_string(), "-c".to_string(), script.to_string()]
}
```

`initializeCommand` is executed on the host (not inside the container), so `/bin/sh` does not exist on Windows. Before #60792 the string was split on whitespace (`args.split(" ")`), so the program was the first token (e.g. `bash`/`echo`), resolved via `PATH`, and host execution worked on Windows. This is a Windows-only regression from #60792. In-container lifecycle commands are unaffected because the Linux container has `/bin/sh`.

### Suggested direction

For commands that run on the host, don't hardcode a POSIX shell. On Windows use the platform shell (`cmd /C` / PowerShell) or resolve the program via `PATH`; reserve `/bin/sh -c` for commands that run inside the container.

### Zed version and system specs

- Zed: v1.23.2+stable.369.c0199504b9cce79bc27524950022ed701bc3ebd5
- OS: Windows 10 Enterprise 10.0.19045
- Architecture: x86_64

body_text:
### Summary

When a native Zed subagent created with `spawn_agent` calls `ask_user`, it blocks waiting for the user to select an answer. However, the subagent is collapsed by default, and there is no visible indication that it is waiting for user input. The user has to discover the pending question by manually expanding the subagent.

This makes the task appear stuck: the parent is waiting for the subagent to finish, while the subagent is waiting for an answer the user has not been alerted to provide.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a thread with the native Zed agent, with `spawn_agent` and `ask_user` enabled.
2. Ask the parent agent to delegate a task to a subagent and have that subagent use `ask_user` to request a decision with selectable options.
3. Leave the subagent collapsed, which is the default presentation.
4. The subagent calls `ask_user` and waits for an answer, but there is no visible prompt or waiting-for-input indication in the parent conversation.
5. Manually expand the subagent to discover the question and select an answer.

### Actual behavior

The pending question is hidden inside the collapsed subagent. There is no indication that user action is required, and progress is blocked until the user discovers and answers it.

This behavior was observed by the reporter. I have not independently reproduced it in this checkout.

### Expected behavior / design question

Should native subagents be able to call `ask_user` at all?

- If subagents are intended to work only through their parent, should `ask_user` be excluded from their available tools, with clarification requests returned to the parent instead?
- If subagents are intended to ask the user directly, is the missing waiting-for-input indication a UI bug? In that case, a pending question should be discoverable without manually expanding every subagent—for example by surfacing the question in the parent conversation, expanding the relevant subagent, or marking its collapsed card as waiting for user input.

Either design seems preferable to silently blocking on a hidden question. Could maintainers clarify the intended behavior?

### Relevant code

Inspected checkout: `56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca` (this identifies the code inspected, not necessarily the installed build exhibiting the issue).

- [`Thread::add_default_tools`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca/crates/agent/src/thread.rs#L2258) registers `AskUserTool` without excluding subagents, while `SpawnAgentTool` is gated by subagent depth.
- [`Thread::new_subagent`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca/crates/agent/src/thread.rs#L1361) reuses the parent project context and templates.
- [`build_request_messages_until`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca/crates/agent/src/thread.rs#L4612) uses the same system prompt template for parent agents and subagents, without a subagent-specific instruction to route questions through the parent.
- [`AskUserTool::run`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca/crates/agent/src/tools/ask_user_tool.rs#L115-L121) requests elicitation and awaits the response.

The native tool is named `ask_user`; this report is about native `spawn_agent` subagents, not Claude Code ACP or its `AskUserQuestion` tool.

### Environment

Exact installed Zed version and model/provider were not captured in this report.

{"repository": "zed-industries/zed", "task_candidate_id": 27119, "repository_id": 319, "issue_number": 65756, "github_issue_id": 5901969632, "html_url": "https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/65756", "created_at": "2026-10-17T18:57:40+00:00", "author_association": null, "title": "Surface pending ask_user questions from collapsed subagents", "body_text": "### Summary

When a native Zed subagent created with `spawn_agent` calls `ask_user`, it blocks waiting for the user to select an answer. However, the subagent is collapsed by default, and there is no visible indication that it is waiting for user input. The user has to discover the pending question by manually expanding the subagent.

This makes the task appear stuck: the parent is waiting for the subagent to finish, while the subagent is waiting for an answer the user has not been alerted to provide.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a thread with the native Zed agent, with `spawn_agent` and `ask_user` enabled.
2. Ask the parent agent to delegate a task to a subagent and have that subagent use `ask_user` to request a decision with selectable options.
3. Leave the subagent collapsed, which is the default presentation.
4. The subagent calls `ask_user` and waits for an answer, but there is no visible prompt or waiting-for-input indication in the parent conversation.
5. Manually expand the subagent to discover the question and select an answer.

### Actual behavior

The pending question is hidden inside the collapsed subagent. There is no indication that user action is required, and progress is blocked until the user discovers and answers it.

This behavior was observed by the reporter. I have not independently reproduced it in this checkout.

### Expected behavior / design question

Should native subagents be able to call `ask_user` at all?

- If subagents are intended to work only through their parent, should `ask_user` be excluded from their available tools, with clarification requests returned to the parent instead?
- If subagents are intended to ask the user directly, is the missing waiting-for-input indication a UI bug? In that case, a pending question should be discoverable without manually expanding every subagent—for example by surfacing the question in the parent conversation, expanding the relevant subagent, or marking its collapsed card as waiting for user input.

Either design seems preferable to silently blocking on a hidden question. Could maintainers clarify the intended behavior?

### Relevant code

Inspected checkout: `56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca` (this identifies the code inspected, not necessarily the installed build exhibiting the issue).

- [`Thread::add_default_tools`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca/crates/agent/src/thread.rs#L2258) registers `AskUserTool` without excluding subagents, while `SpawnAgentTool` is gated by subagent depth.
- [`Thread::new_subagent`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca/crates/agent/src/thread.rs#L1361) reuses the parent project context and templates.
- [`build_request_messages_until`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca/crates/agent/src/thread.rs#L4612) uses the same system prompt template for parent agents and subagents, without a subagent-specific instruction to route questions through the parent.
- [`AskUserTool::run`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/56934ec0560bce8929025497411de7f5322fb6ca/crates/agent/src/tools/ask_user_tool.rs#L115-L121) requests elicitation and awaits the response.

The native tool is named `ask_user`; this report is about native `spawn_agent` subagents, not Claude Code ACP or its `AskUserQuestion` tool.

### Reproduction steps

1. Start Zed with Helix mode
2. Open a file.
3. Press `:sp` to split vertically.
4. Open another file, so that you have two tabs.
5. Press `:quit`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior: The tab closes.
Expected behavior: The whole pane closes (but the buffers/tabs are kept open).

Helix has no concept of tabs. Buffer can remain open, also when not currently displayed anywhere.
To emulate this in Zed, probably the best behavior would be:
1. If there are multiple panes, `:quit` closes the pane, but all uniquely open tabs there are moved to another pane (doesn't matter which).
2. If there is just a single pane open, either `:quit` closes Zed completely or just the last tab.

This is in the same realm of #63845.

body_text:
I'm building a RetroPie rom manager app with GPUI. I was testing an arm64 build on my TV box (s905x3, mali-g31 mp2) running Armbian. App window opened but stayed blank, UI was not rendering. With some help from AI, I managed to trace it to the storage-buffer shaders failing validation on Panfrost’s GL driver. GPUI already has a texture-based path that would work here, but it only turns on for WebGL. I patched that check in my app’s copy of `gpui_wgpu`, and it renders on the board now. It’s slow, but that’s the hardware. The details and logs below were written up with assistance from AI; I’ve tested the fix myself. Happy to open a PR if you want it.

### Reproduction steps

Found in a GPUI app ([retropie-rom-manager](https://github.com/fa-saikat/retropie-rom-installer)), built on the `gpui-pre` 0.3.8 snapshot of `zed@279fe07`. The same code is unchanged on current `main`, so Zed on this hardware should be affected the same way, but I haven't run Zed itself on the board.

1. Use a GPU whose OpenGL ES driver reports no storage buffers in vertex shaders, so wgpu clears `DownlevelFlags::VERTEX_STORAGE`. Mine is a Mali-G31 (Amlogic S905X3) on Panfrost, which has no hardware Vulkan, so wgpu picks the GL adapter.
2. Open any GPUI window.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** The window opens and responds to input, but nothing is drawn. Every frame fails pipeline validation:

```
[INFO  gpui_wgpu::wgpu_context] Selected GPU adapter: "Mali-G31 (Panfrost)" (Gl)
[ERROR gpui_wgpu::wgpu_renderer] GPU error during frame (failure 1 of 10): Validation Error
    Caused by:
      In Device::create_render_pipeline, label = 'poly_sprites'
        PipelineLayout with 'poly_sprites_layout' label is invalid
[ERROR gpui_wgpu::wgpu_renderer] GPU error during frame (failure 2 of 10): Validation Error
    Caused by:
      In Queue::submit
        In a set_pipeline command
          RenderPipeline with 'quads' label is invalid
```

**Expected:** GPUI renders on this adapter, using the texture-based instance data path it already has for WebGL.

**Cause:** The storage-buffer shaders bind instance data as `var<storage>` with `VERTEX_FRAGMENT` visibility, and this driver doesn't allow that. GPUI already has a texture instance path for GPUs like this (`shaders_webgl.wgsl`, `InstanceData::Texture`), and that path is compiled natively. But `uses_webgl_instance_data()` only enables it on wasm:

```rust
// crates/gpui_wgpu/src/wgpu_context.rs
pub fn uses_webgl_instance_data(&self) -> bool {
    matches!(self.backend, WgpuBackend::Gl) && cfg!(target_family = "wasm")
}
```

Natively, the backend is `WgpuBackend::Native(wgpu::Backend::Gl)`, so widening the `matches!` alone isn't enough. This change fixes it on my board:

```rust
pub fn uses_webgl_instance_data(&self) -> bool {
    if cfg!(target_family = "wasm") {
        return matches!(self.backend, WgpuBackend::Gl);
    }
    self.adapter.get_info().backend == wgpu::Backend::Gl
        && !self
            .adapter
            .get_downlevel_capabilities()
            .flags
            .contains(wgpu::DownlevelFlags::VERTEX_STORAGE)
}
```

With it, the log shows the texture path selected, there are no validation errors, and the UI renders on the Mali-G31. I also forced the texture path on llvmpipe's GL on x86_64, and it renders correctly there too. Adapters with vertex storage buffers keep the current path, so nothing changes for them.

I can open a PR with this if it's the direction you'd want.

### Zed version and system specs

Not Zed itself: `gpui-pre-wgpu` 0.3.8 (snapshot of `zed@279fe07`), wgpu 29.0.4. The code is the same on `main`.

- Board: Amlogic S905X3, Mali-G31 (Bifrost)
- OS: Armbian 25.11.0, X11
- Mesa 25.0.7-2+deb13u1 (Panfrost for GL; Vulkan is llvmpipe only)
- Architecture: aarch64

body_text:
### Reproduction steps

1. Set `"max_tabs": 1` in settings.json.
2. Open three files and pin all three.
3. Quit Zed and start it again so the last session is restored.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: only the last pinned tab comes back. The other two are closed while the session is being restored.

Expected: all three pinned tabs are restored. Pinned tabs are exempt from `max_tabs` during normal use (#31870, `test_pinned_tabs_never_closed_at_max_tabs`), and restoring a session should behave the same way.

### Root cause

`SerializedPane::deserialize_to` adds the restored items to the pane one at a time, and it only calls `set_pinned_count` after every item has been added:

- items added in a loop: [`persistence/model.rs#L388-L397`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/1c3d902fbf1cbd513f5d989d96a8c18694e4c287/crates/workspace/src/persistence/model.rs#L388-L397)
- pinned count set afterwards: [`persistence/model.rs#L413-L423`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/1c3d902fbf1cbd513f5d989d96a8c18694e4c287/crates/workspace/src/persistence/model.rs#L413-L423)

Each `add_item` call runs `close_items_on_item_open` first ([`pane.rs#L1243`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/1c3d902fbf1cbd513f5d989d96a8c18694e4c287/crates/workspace/src/pane.rs#L1243)). At that point `pinned_tab_count` is still 0, so `close_items_to_target_count` treats the tabs restored so far as unpinned and evicts them. With `max_tabs: 1`, adding tab 2 closes tab 1 and adding tab 3 closes tab 2.

The pinned count is then calculated from the serialized list, not from the items that survived. So after the restore `pinned_tab_count` is 3 while the pane holds 1 item. `set_pinned_count` doesn't clamp the value ([`pane.rs#L1054`](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/1c3d902fbf1cbd513f5d989d96a8c18694e4c287/crates/workspace/src/pane.rs#L1054)).

### Suggested fix

Mark items as pinned while they are being restored, so the eviction pass sees them as pinned. For each restored item whose serialized index is below `self.pinned_count`, increment the pane's pinned count right after adding it. Then clamp the final count to `pane.items_len()`. Suppressing the `max_tabs` eviction for the whole restore would also work.

### Related

- #31870: pinned tabs closed when going over `max_tabs`. Fixed for normal use, but not for restore.
- #62003: pinned tabs lost after a reload because items failed to deserialize. Different cause, same symptom.
- #41474: pinned tab lost on restart.

### Zed version and system specs

Zed: v1.24.2 (Zed)
OS: macOS 26.6.2
Architecture: aarch64

### Relevant Zed settings

### Reproduction steps 1. Open Zed and navigate to a Git repository with uncommitted changes. 2. Add the following configuration to `settings.json`: ```json { "soft_wrap": "none", "languages": { "Git Commit": { "soft_wrap": "none" } } } ``` 3. Open the Git Panel and enter a commit message containing a line longer than the panel's width, without inserting any newline characters. 4. Observe that the text visually wraps at the panel boundary despite `soft_wrap` being set to `none`. 5. Change the `Git Commit` configuration to: ```json { "soft_wrap": "preferred_line_length", "preferred_line_length": 20 } ``` 6. Observe that wrapping at 20 characters works as expected when the limit is smaller than the panel width. 7. Increase `preferred_line_length` beyond the panel width and repeat the test. The text still wraps at the panel boundary rather than continuing horizontally. This appears related to #44748 and its fix in #46422, which was merged on February 5, 2026. ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current behavior** The Git Panel commit editor always visually wraps long lines at the panel boundary, even with `soft_wrap: "none"`. The `preferred_line_length` setting is partially respected: values smaller than the panel width work correctly, but values larger than the panel width do not prevent wrapping at the panel boundary. I have verified that these are visual soft wraps, not actual newline characters in the commit message. **Expected behavior** With `soft_wrap: "none"`, the Git Panel commit editor should not visually wrap lines at the panel boundary. Long lines should remain on a single logical and visual line, with horizontal scrolling if necessary. With `soft_wrap: "preferred_line_length"`, wrapping should follow the configured column limit rather than always being constrained to the panel width. **Additional context** PR #46422 explicitly addressed the Git Panel commit editor not respecting soft-wrap settings. However, the behavior described above is still reproducible in Zed 1.24.2 on Windows 11 (in my case, when working with a repository hosted in WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04)). ### Zed version and system specs Zed: 1.24.2 (Stable) Commit: `fb69067729cb16a7f6135e2c1600c26a2c59659` Version: `1.24.2+stable.373.fb69067729cb16a7f6135e2c1600c26a2c59659` OS: Windows 11 Architecture: x86_64 Repository environment: WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04 ### Attach Zed log file
Zed.log ```log ```

### Reproduction steps

When Zed is launched from the GNOME dash, zed-editor and everything it spawns stay in org.gnome.Shell@user.service instead of an app scope. You can see this in Zed's terminal:

```
$ cat /proc/self/cgroup
0::/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/session.slice/org.gnome.Shell@user.service
```

That unit has OOMPolicy=stop. When the kernel OOM-killed a memory-heavy process started from Zed's terminal, systemd stopped gnome-shell and the whole session ended.

**Cause**
The desktop entry runs the CLI. The CLI forks zed-editor (boot_background in crates/cli/src/main.rs) and exits. GNOME Shell creates the app scope asynchronously, for the launched PID only, so the already-forked editor stays behind. This is a known race in GNOME: gnome-shell#7466 (https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-shell/-/work_items/7466). Other apps don't hit it: Chromium/Electron apps such as VS Code move themselves into their own scope at startup, and Ptyxis/VTE start each terminal in its own scope.

**Proposal**
On Linux with systemd, Zed could place itself in its own scope (from the CLI before exec, or from the editor at startup), and start each terminal in its own scope. The second part would also fix #63724.

When Zed is launched from the GNOME dash, zed-editor and everything it spawns stay in org.gnome.Shell@user.service instead of an app scope. You can see this in Zed's terminal:

```
$ cat /proc/self/cgroup
0::/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/session.slice/org.gnome.Shell@user.service
```

That unit has OOMPolicy=stop. When the kernel OOM-killed a memory-heavy process started from Zed's terminal, systemd stopped gnome-shell and the whole session ended.

**Cause**
The desktop entry runs the CLI. The CLI forks zed-editor (boot_background in crates/cli/src/main.rs) and exits. GNOME Shell creates the app scope asynchronously, for the launched PID only, so the already-forked editor stays behind. This is a known race in GNOME: gnome-shell#7466 (https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-shell/-/work_items/7466). Other apps don't hit it: Chromium/Electron apps such as VS Code move themselves into their own scope at startup, and Ptyxis/VTE start each terminal in its own scope.

**Proposal**
On Linux with systemd, Zed could place itself in its own scope (from the CLI before exec, or from the editor at startup), and start each terminal in its own scope. The second part would also fix #63724.

### Reproduction steps

This is a GPUI bug (Windows platform), found in a GPUI app outside Zed. Zed itself can hit it wherever it posts a system notification (e.g. agent notifications).

1. In a GPUI app on Windows, open a window.
2. From a foreground task, post a notification while `App` is borrowed, for example:

```rust
cx.spawn(async move |cx| {
    cx.background_executor().timer(Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
    cx.update(|cx| {
        cx.show_system_notification(SystemNotification {
            tag: "test".into(),
            title: "Hello".into(),
            body: "From a GPUI task".into(),
            actions: vec![],
        });
    });
})
.detach();
```

3. Run with logging on, and watch the log when the toast appears.

(The snippet is a reduced form of what our app does; our app posts the notification from inside an `Entity::update` in such a task. We saw the errors in that app; we haven't run this exact snippet on its own.)

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the toast is shown, but every time one appears GPUI logs a burst of errors:

```
[2026-10-18T21:09:25Z ERROR] RefCell already borrowed
[2026-10-18T21:09:25Z ERROR] RefCell already borrowed
... (9 lines for the first toast, about 3 for each later one)
```

Those window callbacks are dropped. Nothing visibly broke in our tests, but the window's active/hover state can go stale.

**Expected:** showing a notification doesn't make GPUI drop window callbacks.

**Likely cause:** `WindowsPlatform::show_system_notification` (`crates/gpui_windows/src/platform.rs`) calls `ToastNotifier::Show` synchronously while `App` is borrowed. Showing the toast changes window activation and hover state, and Windows delivers those messages straight into GPUI's wndproc. The callbacks registered in `Window::new` (`on_active_status_change`, `on_hover_status_change`, …) then call `handle.update(&mut cx, …)`, which fails to borrow `App`, and `.log_err()` prints the message.

It's the same class of problem as #61789 (the deferred `on_appearance_changed`) and the closed draft #56168 (`update_or_defer`). Possible fixes: post the toast from a deferred foreground task, or defer these window callbacks when `App` is borrowed.

The code is unchanged on `main`: `system_notifications.rs` was last touched in #61189, and `on_active_status_change` in `crates/gpui/src/window.rs` still updates synchronously.

### Zed version and system specs

Not Zed itself: GPUI from Zed rev `93d745668805029476e6d7fbb19652116fed51de` (2026-10-12), via the `gpui-pre` 0.3.9 snapshot. Windows 11, Intel Arc A580 (Direct3D 11.1), app run as an unpackaged exe.

### Summary

With `on_new_window: "launchpad"`, clicking the Dock icon while Zed is running with **no windows** shows the Launchpad the first time — but on the next Dock-icon reopen, a stale empty **untitled** buffer window is restored instead of the Launchpad.

### Steps to trigger the problem

1. Start from these settings (`on_new_window` is already the default in recent versions):

```json
{
  "on_new_window": "launchpad",
  "when_closing_with_no_tabs": "close_window",
  "on_last_window_closed": "platform_default"
}
```

2. Open a project.
3. Close the window with <kbd>Cmd-W</kbd>. With `when_closing_with_no_tabs: "close_window"` the window closes and the app stays running with zero windows (macOS default for `on_last_window_closed`).
4. Click the Zed Dock icon → the **Launchpad** appears. ✅
5. Open a project again (from the Launchpad).
6. Close its window again with <kbd>Cmd-W</kbd>.
7. Click the Zed Dock icon again → an empty **untitled** buffer window appears instead of the Launchpad. ❌

This is reproducible: the first reopen after launching Zed shows the Launchpad; reopens after a Launchpad → open project → close cycle restore an untitled buffer instead.

### Actual Behavior

Reopening Zed from the Dock while it is running with zero windows does not consistently honor `on_new_window: "launchpad"`. After the first Launchpad → open project → close cycle, something that looks like a serialized untitled workspace gets restored from the session store, overriding the Launchpad.

### Expected Behavior

Dock-icon reopen with zero windows should always honor `on_new_window` and show the Launchpad, regardless of how many Launchpad → open project → close cycles happened before.

### Hypothesis

The reopen path restores the last persisted workspace session before/instead of applying `on_new_window`. The first reopen works because no untitled workspace exists in the session store yet; a later cycle persists one, and from then on reopens restore it.

### Workaround

Setting `"on_last_window_closed": "quit_app"` avoids the buggy state entirely: the app never sits around with zero windows, so a Dock click is always a fresh launch, which shows the Launchpad correctly.

### Related issues

- #47075 — Restore to Launchpad not taking effect
- #60720 — New Window ignores `restore_on_startup: "launchpad"`
- #63303 — Launchpad briefly flashes before restored untitled window on relaunch from Dock
- #50103 — "Close project" still leaves an Untitled buffer open

### Zed Version and System Details

body_text:
## Observations

Remote development over SSH to an ARM64 Linux VM running in UTM on macOS.
The VM has 8 vCPUs.

Four remote crash-handler processes were running alongside the workspace and setup server/proxy processes.
A short strace showed a crash handler repeatedly calling timerfd_settime with approximately 10 ms timeouts and waiting in epoll_pwait.

| Measurement | Zed connected | After quitting Zed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS VM process CPU (100% = one core) | 35–39% | ~11% |
| Guest timer interrupts/sec | ~1,333 | ~240 |
| Guest CPU idle across 8 vCPUs | 96% | 99.3% |

The VM remained running, and all remote Zed processes exited after quitting Zed.
These are short samples, not a battery-runtime benchmark.

The minidumper polling loop contains a hardcoded 10 ms timeout:
https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/crash-handling/blob/main/minidumper/src/ipc/server.rs

This maybe by design, but is a bit of a bummer when using Zed against a local VM, I imagine a popular setup for Linux engineers working on a mac book pro. 

Took me a bit to find out what was draining battery life, since these laptops are so efficient normally.

Anyway, maybe at a minimum we can get some advanced config options to tune these polling intervals?

body_text:
### Bug Description

When joining a code line with a trailing comment line using `J` (or `:j`), Zed strips the comment prefix from the second line, producing invalid code.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a C/C++ file
2. Place the cursor on the first line
3. Press `J`

```c
CMIS_MEDIA_TYPE_UNDEFINED = 0,
// Undefined
```


### Actual Result

```c
CMIS_MEDIA_TYPE_UNDEFINED = 0,  Undefined
```

The `//` prefix is removed, leaving bare text in the code.

### Expected Result

```c
CMIS_MEDIA_TYPE_UNDEFINED = 0, // Undefined
```

The comment prefix should be preserved because the first line is not a comment — the join should simply concatenate the lines.



### Context

The comment-aware join feature (from #4481) is intended for joining two consecutive comment lines:

```c
// This is
// a comment
```
→ `// This is a comment`

However, the prefix-stripping logic does not check whether the **first** line is itself a comment before removing the prefix from the second. It should only strip when both lines are comments.


### Zed version and system specs

- Zed 1.24.3 (vim-mode)
- OS: Arch Linux
- Language: C, Zig
